Amazon Polly converts text to synthesised speech, Amazon Translate performs language translation between languages, and Amazon Transcribe converts spoken audio into text transcripts. None of these services are designed for document analysis or information extraction.

text: A telecom support team wants to study what customers talk about during recorded phone calls and pull out the important points. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: Create classification labels with Amazon Comprehend
Build a conversational chatbot with Amazon Lex
Convert the call recordings to text with Amazon Transcribe
Extract information from the recordings with Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor
explanation:
Amazon Transcribe converts the speech in the call recordings into text, which the team can then analyze to pull out the key information discussed.
Amazon Comprehend analyzes text for insights such as classification, but it needs text rather than raw audio as input. Amazon Lex builds conversational chatbots and does not transcribe existing recordings. Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor watches deployed models for drift and has nothing to do with audio transcription.

text: At which stage of the ML lifecycle are regulatory and compliance obligations primarily established?
explanation:
Regulatory and compliance obligations are primarily established during business goal identification, because defining what you want to build determines which laws and regulations apply to the project before any data is collected or processed.
Data collection is where those obligations are applied in practice, such as obtaining consent and verifying data sources, but the obligations themselves must be understood before collection begins. Model training and feature engineering are later technical stages focused on building and optimizing the model, not on identifying the legal and regulatory framework that governs the project.

text: A streaming service studies subscriber habits and demographics to suggest tailored shows. After putting its custom model into production, the team needs to watch whether the model's quality declines over time. Which AWS service or feature meets these requirements?
explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor continuously tracks a deployed model in production and detects drift and quality degradation over time, which is what the team needs to watch as subscriber behavior changes.
Amazon SageMaker Clarify focuses on bias and explainability, while Amazon Comprehend and Amazon Rekognition are managed services for text and image analysis, none of which monitor a deployed model for quality drift.

text: An organization runs many ML models in production and needs to know when any of them starts behaving differently from its baseline so the team can step in. Which AWS service or feature meets these requirements?
explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor continuously measures data and prediction quality for deployed models and alerts when they deviate from a baseline, letting the organization detect and resolve quality changes quickly.
Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler prepares data, Amazon SageMaker JumpStart provides pre-built models, and Amazon SageMaker HyperPod provides distributed training infrastructure; none of these monitors deployed models for quality changes.

text: After producing a number of ML models, a team needs one place to keep them, manage them, and track each version. Which AWS service or feature meets these requirements?
explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Model Registry is a central repository for storing, managing, and versioning ML models and tracking their deployment status across the lifecycle, which meets the team's needs.
Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor detects drift in deployed models, Amazon SageMaker Canvas builds models with a no-code interface, and AWS Audit Manager collects audit evidence; none of these is the service for model versioning and management.

text: While watching a predictive model with Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor, a team sees data drift cross the threshold it had set. The team wants to limit any harm this could cause the model. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: Re-train the model with fresh data
explanation:
When data drift passes the defined threshold, the data no longer matches what the model was trained on, so re-training the model with fresh data restores its accuracy and limits the negative impact.
Adjusting the monitoring sensitivity only changes when alerts fire, restarting the endpoint does not address the changed data, and setting up experiment tracking records runs without correcting the drift.

text: Why do teams monitor models once they are running in production?
options: To detect issues such as model drift or data drift
explanation:
The primary purpose of model monitoring in production is to detect issues such as model drift or data drift so teams can act before performance degrades.
Collecting more data, performing feature engineering, and training new models are separate lifecycle activities, not the purpose of monitoring a deployed model.

text: Which task is Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor designed to perform?
options: To detect data drift and model performance degradation
explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor continuously watches deployed models and detects data drift and model performance degradation, alerting teams when investigation or retraining is needed.
Serving models for inference, creating training datasets, and training models faster are handled by other capabilities and are not the purpose of Model Monitor.

text: An online store wants to tailor its recommendations to each individual shopper. Which AWS service fits?
explanation:
Amazon Personalize builds machine learning models from user behavior to deliver individualized recommendations, which is exactly what tailoring results per shopper requires.
Amazon Comprehend analyzes text, Amazon Kendra provides enterprise search, and Amazon Rekognition analyzes images and video; none personalizes recommendations per user.

text: A company needs to produce its product descriptions in several languages automatically. Which AWS service does this?
explanation:
Amazon Translate uses neural machine translation to convert text between languages automatically, which is what generating product descriptions in multiple languages requires.
Amazon Polly converts text to speech, Amazon Comprehend extracts insights from text, and Amazon Transcribe converts speech to text; none translates text.

text: A hospital wants an AI application that reads structured patient records, extracts the relevant clinical details, and produces concise summaries. Which solution fits?
options: Use Amazon Personalize to model patient engagement and pass the output to a general model
Use Amazon Comprehend Medical to extract medical entities and relationships, then apply rule-based logic to format the summaries
Use Amazon Textract to digitize scanned documents, then run keyword extraction
Use Amazon Kendra to index the records for search, then apply a template
explanation:
Amazon Comprehend Medical is purpose-built to extract medical entities and relationships from clinical text, and applying rule-based logic afterward formats the information into concise summaries, meeting both needs.
Amazon Personalize models engagement for recommendations, Amazon Textract digitizes documents without interpreting clinical meaning, and Amazon Kendra indexes content for search rather than extracting structured clinical entities.

text: A company has built custom Computer Vision models and needs an easy-to-use interface for labeling data to reduce errors on new, real-world images. Which AWS tool fits?
explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth provides a built-in labeling interface with workflows and quality controls for tasks such as Computer Vision, producing high-quality labeled data that reduces model errors.
SageMaker Canvas is a no-code interface for building models, Rekognition Custom Labels trains a model rather than offering a general labeling interface, and SageMaker Autopilot auto-builds models from tabular data.

text: A bank deployed an ML model to predict customer churn and wants to measure how accurately it predicts churn compared with actual behavior. Which metric fits?
explanation:
The F1 score balances precision and recall, which makes it well suited to measuring accuracy on a binary classification task such as predicting whether a customer will churn.
RMSE measures error for regression predictions, ROI is a business-value metric, and perplexity measures language-modeling fit; none fits binary churn classification.

text: Which two capabilities make Amazon Kendra valuable for enterprise search applications?
explanation:
Amazon Kendra provides natural language understanding that interprets user intent and semantic search that returns results by meaning and context, which together make it effective for enterprise search.
Managed relational database hosting, video transcoding, and infrastructure monitoring are unrelated tasks that Kendra does not perform.

text: A model's inference quality dropped after four months in production. The team wants alerts if quality degrades again and to prevent recurrence. Which solution fits?
options: Build a new model and monitor drift with Amazon SageMaker Feature Store
Retrain the model and monitor drift with Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor
Retrain the model and monitor drift with Amazon SageMaker Clarify
Build a new model and watch it with Amazon CloudWatch alarms only
explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor continuously detects data and model drift in production and can send alerts, so the team is notified and can retrain before quality degrades again.
SageMaker Clarify focuses on bias and explainability, SageMaker Feature Store stores features, and CloudWatch alarms track infrastructure metrics but do not detect model drift on their own.

text: An online learning company has large volumes of educational material and wants enterprise search across it. Which AWS service fits?
explanation:
Amazon Kendra is an intelligent enterprise search service that searches large volumes of unstructured content, such as educational materials, which fits this need.
Amazon Polly converts text to speech, Amazon Textract extracts text from documents, and Amazon Comprehend analyzes text for insights; none provides enterprise search.

text: A company is building an ML model with Amazon SageMaker and needs to share and manage variables used for model development across several teams. Which SageMaker feature meets this requirement?
explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Feature Store is a centralized repository for storing, sharing, and reusing features, which lets multiple teams manage the same variables for model development.
Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler prepares and transforms data, Amazon SageMaker Clarify detects bias and supports explainability, and Amazon SageMaker Model Cards document model details. None of these is designed to share and manage features across teams.

text: A company deployed a deep learning model for object detection to production. When the model examines a new image to identify the objects in it, which AI process is taking place?
explanation:
Inference is the process in which a deployed model analyzes new data, such as a new image, to produce a prediction, so identifying objects in an incoming image is inference.
Training is the earlier process of fitting the model to data, model deployment is making the trained model available to serve requests, and bias correction adjusts for unfair outcomes. None of these describes analyzing a new image to make a prediction.

text: A company wants to find harmful language in the comments on social media posts and does not plan to use labeled data to train a model. Which approach should the company use?
options: Use Amazon SageMaker built-in algorithms to train a model
Use Amazon Polly to monitor the comments
explanation:
Amazon Comprehend provides pre-trained natural language processing, including toxicity detection, so it can identify harmful language in comments without the company having to label data or train a model.
Amazon Rekognition moderates images and video, not text. Amazon SageMaker built-in algorithms would require labeled data to train a model. Amazon Polly converts text to speech and does not analyze text for harmful content.

text: A practitioner with limited ML experience wants to predict employee attrition without writing any code. Which Amazon SageMaker feature meets this requirement?
explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Canvas offers a no-code visual interface that lets a user with limited ML experience build, train, and generate predictions, such as employee attrition, without writing code.
SageMaker Clarify detects bias and explains predictions, SageMaker Model Monitor tracks deployed models for drift, and SageMaker Data Wrangler prepares data. None of these provides a no-code way to build a predictive model.

text: A bank must provide regulators with a clear explanation of every factor that influenced each loan decision. The team is choosing between a gradient boosting model and a large language model. Which factor most strongly favors using the traditional ML model?
explanation:
Traditional ML models such as gradient boosting produce outputs that can be traced back to specific input features and their weights, making them well suited to regulated environments where every decision must be fully explainable to auditors and regulators.
Multilingual support and conversational interface needs are strengths of foundation models, not reasons to choose traditional ML. Content generation capability is a defining feature of generative AI and is irrelevant to a loan-decision model that classifies applications rather than generating text.

text: A healthcare startup wants to deploy a diagnostic support tool that must run on devices with limited memory and no internet connection. Which constraint most strongly favors a traditional ML model over a foundation model?
options: The need for real-time image generation
Operational constraints on memory and connectivity
The requirement for multilingual chat support
The desire for open-ended text summarization
explanation:
Traditional ML models are typically much smaller and can run efficiently on resource-constrained edge devices without requiring cloud connectivity, making them the appropriate choice when operational constraints such as limited memory and offline operation apply.
Real-time image generation, multilingual chat support, and open-ended text summarization are capabilities that favor foundation models, not constraints that would lead a team to choose traditional ML.

text: A logistics company processes thousands of delivery route requests each day. Which benefit does AI/ML provide that a purely rule-based system cannot easily achieve?
options: Ability to scale and adapt to changing patterns in the data
explanation:
AI/ML systems learn patterns from data and can adapt as those patterns change over time, and they scale to handle large volumes of requests by generalizing from examples rather than requiring manually coded rules for every scenario, which is a key advantage over rule-based systems.
Deterministic outputs are actually a characteristic of rule-based systems, not a unique benefit of AI/ML. No system can guarantee correctness without validation. AI/ML does not eliminate computational costs; in fact, training and inference often require significant compute resources.

text: A retailer wants to personalize product recommendations for millions of customers. Why is AI/ML more suitable than a manual approach for this task?
options: AI/ML removes the need for any data
AI/ML can process large volumes of data and identify patterns humans cannot easily detect
AI/ML guarantees 100% accuracy on every prediction
AI/ML eliminates the need for computing infrastructure
explanation:
AI/ML excels at processing large volumes of customer data, identifying subtle patterns and preferences, and generating personalized recommendations at a scale that would be impractical for humans to achieve manually, which is why it adds value for this use case.
AI/ML requires data to learn from, so it does not remove the need for any data. No system guarantees 100% accuracy. AI/ML requires computing infrastructure for training and inference, so it does not eliminate infrastructure needs.

text: A startup wants to use a foundation model for its application but lacks the data and resources to train one from scratch. Which approach allows the team to obtain a foundation model without pre-training it themselves?
options: Use an open-source pre-trained model from a model hub
Build a rule-based expert system instead
Collect more labeled data and train a decision tree
Write custom inference code without any model
explanation:
Open-source pre-trained models are available from model hubs and can be used directly or fine-tuned for specific tasks, allowing teams to leverage foundation models without the massive data and compute resources required to pre-train them from scratch.
Building a rule-based expert system does not provide a foundation model. Training a decision tree creates a traditional ML model, not a foundation model. Writing custom inference code without any model provides no predictive capability at all.

text: A company wants to experiment with multiple foundation models before selecting one for production. Which AWS service provides access to a variety of pre-trained foundation models from different providers?
explanation:
Amazon SageMaker JumpStart provides access to a variety of pre-trained foundation models from AWS and third-party providers, allowing teams to experiment with different models and deploy them with minimal setup, which directly addresses the company's need.
Amazon Personalize builds recommendation models from user interaction data rather than providing access to general-purpose foundation models. Amazon Comprehend is a managed NLP service for text analysis. Amazon Transcribe converts speech to text. None of these provides a catalog of foundation models from multiple providers.

text: An enterprise is modernizing legacy applications and wants an AWS service that helps transform and migrate workloads using AI-assisted tooling. Which AWS service meets this requirement?
explanation:
AWS Transform is an AWS service that uses AI-assisted tooling to help enterprises transform and modernize their legacy applications and workloads, which directly meets the company's requirement.
Amazon Textract extracts text and data from documents. Amazon Translate converts text between languages. Amazon Transcribe converts speech to text. None of these is designed for application modernization and transformation.

text: Which description best defines agentic AI?
options: AI that generates images from text prompts
AI that autonomously plans, decides, and takes actions to achieve goals
AI that converts speech to text
AI that groups similar data points into clusters
explanation:
Agentic AI refers to AI systems that can autonomously plan, make decisions, and take actions to accomplish goals, often by using tools, managing memory, and orchestrating multi-step workflows without constant human direction.
Generating images from text prompts describes diffusion models or image-generation AI. Converting speech to text describes speech recognition. Grouping similar data points into clusters describes unsupervised learning techniques like K-means.

text: How does agentic AI differ from traditional AI systems?
options: Agentic AI requires more training data than traditional AI
Agentic AI can only process text, while traditional AI handles all data types
Agentic AI can autonomously execute multi-step tasks, while traditional AI typically responds to single requests
Agentic AI is always more accurate than traditional AI
explanation:
Agentic AI systems can autonomously break down goals into steps, use tools, and execute multi-step workflows to achieve objectives, whereas traditional AI systems typically process individual requests and return single responses without autonomous planning or action-taking.
Agentic AI does not inherently require more training data than traditional AI. Agentic AI can work with multiple data types, not just text. Accuracy depends on the specific model and task, not on whether the system is agentic.

text: A development team wants an AI assistant that can answer questions about their codebase, explain existing code, and help troubleshoot issues directly in their IDE. Which AWS service meets this requirement?
explanation:
Amazon Q Developer is an AI-powered assistant that integrates with IDEs to answer questions about code, explain how existing code works, and help developers troubleshoot issues, which matches what the team needs.
Amazon Comprehend analyzes text for sentiment and entities but does not assist with code. Amazon Textract extracts text from documents and images. Amazon Transcribe converts speech to text. None of these provides code-aware assistance in an IDE.

text: A software team wants to use AI to help define requirements, generate design documents, and implement features based on specifications. Which AWS service supports this spec-driven development workflow?
explanation:
Kiro is an AI-powered development environment that supports spec-driven development, helping teams define requirements, generate design documents, and implement features based on specifications.
Amazon Personalize generates recommendations based on user behavior. Amazon Rekognition analyzes images and video. Amazon Polly converts text to speech. None of these supports spec-driven software development workflows.

text: A business analyst wants to create interactive dashboards with AI-generated insights and natural language querying of data. Which AWS service meets this requirement?
explanation:
Amazon Quick (formerly Amazon QuickSight Q) provides AI-powered business intelligence with natural language querying, allowing business analysts to ask questions in plain language and receive visualizations and insights from their data.
Amazon Athena runs SQL queries on data in Amazon S3 but does not provide AI-generated insights or natural language querying. Amazon Redshift is a data warehouse for analytics workloads. AWS Glue is a data integration service for ETL jobs. None of these offers the AI-powered natural language business intelligence experience.

text: A contact center wants to build a voice-enabled virtual agent that understands customer requests and routes calls to the appropriate department. Which AWS service meets this requirement?
explanation:
Amazon Lex is a service for building conversational interfaces using voice and text, enabling the contact center to create a virtual agent that understands spoken requests and can route calls based on customer intent.
Amazon Polly converts text to speech but does not understand or interpret spoken input. Amazon Translate converts text between languages. Amazon Comprehend extracts insights from text but does not build interactive conversational agents.

text: A law firm has thousands of legal documents and wants employees to find relevant case law and contract clauses using natural language questions. Which type of AI application best addresses this need?
explanation:
A knowledge base application uses AI to index, understand, and retrieve information from large document collections, allowing users to find relevant content by asking natural language questions, which is exactly what the law firm needs for searching legal documents.
Fraud detection identifies suspicious transactions or activities. Time series forecasting predicts future values from historical sequential data. Anomaly detection flags unusual patterns in data. None of these enables natural language search across document collections.

text: What does the term Large Language Model (LLM) refer to?
options: A database that stores large amounts of text
A deep learning model trained on vast text data to understand and generate human language
A tool for translating between programming languages
A system that converts speech to text
explanation:
A Large Language Model (LLM) is a deep learning model trained on massive amounts of text data that can understand context, generate coherent text, answer questions, and perform various language tasks.
A database stores data but does not understand or generate language. A programming language translator converts code syntax, not natural language understanding. A speech-to-text system transcribes audio but is not what the term LLM describes.

text: Which statement best describes Generative AI?
options: AI that only classifies data into predefined categories
AI that creates new content such as text, images, or audio based on learned patterns
AI that exclusively detects anomalies in datasets
AI that only retrieves existing information from databases
explanation:
Generative AI refers to AI systems that can create new content, including text, images, audio, video, and code, by learning patterns from training data and generating novel outputs that resemble that data.
Classifying data into predefined categories describes classification models, not generative models. Detecting anomalies describes anomaly detection systems. Retrieving existing information describes search or retrieval systems. None of these involves creating new content.

text: A company wants an AI system that can autonomously research competitors, compile findings into a report, and email the summary to stakeholders without human intervention at each step. Which type of AI application best fits this requirement?
explanation:
Agentic AI can autonomously plan and execute multi-step workflows, such as researching information, compiling reports, and sending emails, without requiring human intervention at each step, which matches the company's requirement.
Speech recognition converts spoken audio to text. Image classification assigns labels to images. Sentiment analysis determines the emotional tone of text. None of these can autonomously orchestrate multi-step tasks across different systems.

text: Which statement best describes how Deep Learning differs from traditional Machine Learning?
options: Deep Learning requires manually engineered features, while traditional Machine Learning does not
Deep Learning uses multi-layered neural networks that automatically learn feature representations from raw data
Deep Learning can only be applied to text data
Deep Learning always requires less data than traditional Machine Learning
explanation:
Deep Learning uses neural networks with many layers that automatically discover useful feature representations directly from raw data, removing the need for manual feature engineering that traditional Machine Learning typically requires.
Traditional Machine Learning is the approach that usually depends on manually engineered features, so option A reverses the relationship. Deep Learning applies to images, audio, text, and other data types, not only text. Deep Learning generally requires more data than traditional Machine Learning because its multi-layered networks have many more parameters to train.

text: A retail chain wants to automatically detect and blur customer faces in its security camera footage before storing the recordings. Which AWS service meets this requirement?
explanation:
Amazon Rekognition is a Computer Vision service that can detect, analyze, and identify faces in images and video, so it can locate customer faces in security footage for the company to blur before storage.
Amazon Textract extracts text and structured data from documents and images but does not detect faces. Amazon Comprehend is a Natural Language Processing service that analyzes text for sentiment, entities, and key phrases. Amazon Transcribe converts spoken audio into text. None of these provides facial detection in video.

text: Which of the following is an example of unstructured data?
options: A database table of customer orders with columns for date, quantity, and price
A spreadsheet listing employee IDs, names, and salaries
A collection of free-form customer support emails
A CSV file containing sensor readings indexed by timestamp
explanation:
Free-form customer support emails are unstructured data because they have no predefined schema or fixed format: the content varies in length, style, and layout, making them unsuitable for direct storage in rows and columns without processing.
A database table with defined columns, a spreadsheet with named fields, and a CSV file with consistent columns are all examples of structured data because each record follows a predefined schema where every field has a known type and position.

text: In the context of MLOps, what does managing technical debt refer to?
options: Reducing the financial cost of cloud compute instances
Addressing accumulated shortcuts, outdated dependencies, and undocumented processes that make ML systems harder to maintain over time
Increasing the number of model parameters to improve accuracy
Deleting old datasets that are no longer needed
explanation:
Technical debt in MLOps refers to the accumulated cost of shortcuts, poorly documented pipelines, outdated dependencies, and tightly coupled components that make ML systems progressively harder to maintain, extend, and debug over time. Managing it means proactively refactoring, documenting, and modernizing these systems.
Reducing cloud compute costs is cost optimization, not technical debt management. Increasing model parameters is a modeling decision related to capacity, not maintenance burden. Deleting old datasets is a data governance activity rather than a response to accumulated engineering shortcuts.

text: A data science team runs dozens of training jobs with different configurations each week. It needs to compare results and reproduce any previous run. Which MLOps practice meets this requirement?
explanation:
Experiment tracking records the parameters, metrics, code versions, and artifacts for every training run, allowing the team to compare results across runs and reproduce any previous experiment exactly, which supports the MLOps principles of experimentation and repeatable processes.
Model deployment is the process of making a trained model available for inference and does not record or compare training configurations. Data labeling assigns ground-truth annotations to training examples, not to tracking the outcomes of training jobs. Feature serving delivers pre-computed features to models at inference time and has nothing to do with recording training experiment details.

text: What is the purpose of hyperparameter tuning in the ML development lifecycle?
options: To collect and clean the raw training data
To find the model configuration settings that produce the best performance
To deploy the trained model to a production endpoint
To monitor the model for data drift after deployment
explanation:
Hyperparameter tuning searches for the optimal configuration settings, such as learning rate, batch size, and number of layers, that are set before training begins and directly influence model performance. Finding the best combination maximizes the model's accuracy or other target metric.
Collecting and cleaning raw data is the data collection and preprocessing stage. Deploying the model to a production endpoint is the deployment stage. Monitoring for data drift is part of the post-deployment monitoring stage. Each of these is a separate step in the ML lifecycle.

text: In Machine Learning, what does the term bias most commonly refer to?
options: The speed at which a model trains
A systematic error that causes a model to consistently favor certain outcomes over others
The total number of parameters in a model
The process of splitting data into training and test sets
explanation:
In Machine Learning, bias refers to a systematic error where the model consistently skews toward certain predictions or outcomes, which can arise from unrepresentative training data, flawed assumptions in the algorithm, or imbalanced datasets. Identifying and reducing bias is essential for building fair and accurate models.
Training speed is a measure of computational performance, not bias. The total number of parameters describes model capacity or complexity. Splitting data into training and test sets is a data preparation step called train-test splitting. None of these relates to the concept of systematic prediction error.

text: A team has trained a model to predict customer churn. The model is highly accurate on the training data but predicts poorly on new, unseen customers. Which change will resolve this?
options: Reduce the regularization strength so the model can fit more complex patterns
Add further features to the input dataset
Continue training the model for more epochs
Increase the regularization strength so the model becomes less complex
explanation:
The model is overfitting: it has effectively memorised the training data and fails to generalise to new, unseen customers. Increasing the regularization strength penalises large weights and reduces model complexity, which encourages a simpler model that captures general patterns rather than noise, closing the gap between training and real-world performance.
Reducing the regularization strength would increase model complexity and make the overfitting worse. Adding further input features also tends to increase complexity, again worsening generalisation. Continuing training for more epochs lets the model fit the training data even more closely, which deepens the overfitting rather than resolving it.

text: A retail company built a model to forecast product prices. It scored very well on the training dataset, but once it was released to production its accuracy dropped sharply. What should the company do to address this problem?
options: Train the model for a longer period of time
Increase the amount of data used for training
Reduce the amount of data used for training
Add more hyperparameters to the model
explanation:
Strong results on the training set paired with a sharp drop in production is the classic signature of overfitting, where the model has memorised the training examples instead of learning general patterns. Training on a larger and more varied dataset helps the model generalise to unseen data and closes the gap between training and production performance.
Reducing the training data leaves the model even less to learn from and usually makes overfitting and poor generalisation worse. Adding more hyperparameters increases model complexity, which tends to deepen overfitting rather than relieve it. Training for longer simply fits the existing training data more tightly and does nothing to improve performance on new data, so it does not solve the generalisation problem.

text: A publisher needs to turn long research reports into short briefs that capture their main points, using a large language model (LLM). Which solution meets this requirement?
options: Build a named entity recognition system
explanation:
A summarization chatbot uses an LLM to read long documents and produce a shorter version that keeps the essential points, which is exactly what condensing research reports into briefs requires.
A recommendation engine suggests relevant items from user behavior and does not condense documents. A named entity recognition system only pulls out entities such as names, dates, and places rather than producing a coherent summary. A multi-language translation system converts text between languages without shortening or distilling the content.

text: A smart-home device maker wants its appliances to run language-model inference on the device itself, with the lowest latency possible. Which solution meets this requirement?
options: Deploy optimized large language models (LLMs) on the edge devices
Deploy optimized small language models (SLMs) on the edge devices
Call a centralized small language model (SLM) API asynchronously from the edge devices
Call a centralized large language model (LLM) API asynchronously from the edge devices
explanation:
Deploying optimized small language models (SLMs) on the edge devices keeps inference local and avoids network round-trips, which delivers the lowest possible latency, and SLMs are compact enough to run on constrained edge hardware.
Deploying LLMs on edge devices is impractical because their size and compute demands exceed typical edge hardware and would raise latency. Calling a centralized SLM or LLM API requires network communication, and the asynchronous round-trips add latency rather than minimizing it.

text: A fintech engineering team plans to adopt Amazon Q Developer to ship features faster. What can Amazon Q Developer do to help the team?
options: Run an application without provisioning or managing servers
Convert audio files into text documents by using ML models
Generate code snippets and provide reference tracking and open source license tracking
Enable voice commands for coding and natural-language search
explanation:
Amazon Q Developer boosts developer productivity by generating code snippets and providing reference tracking and open source license tracking.
Running an application without provisioning or managing servers describes serverless compute such as AWS Lambda. Converting audio files into text describes Amazon Transcribe. Enabling voice commands for coding is not a function of Amazon Q Developer.

text: An ecommerce team is building visual search that accepts both a typed phrase and a product photo as the query. Which kind of foundation model (FM) should power it?
explanation:
A multimodal embedding model encodes both text and images into a shared vector space, so queries of either type can be compared and matched, which is what a search application handling text and image queries needs.
A text embedding model handles only text. An image generation model creates images from prompts rather than encoding queries for search. A multimodal generation model produces new content across modalities rather than the embeddings needed for similarity search.

text: A marketing agency is exploring generative AI. Which of these tasks is a generative AI use case?
options: Improving network security by using an intrusion detection system
Forecasting stock market trends from historical financial data
Generating photorealistic images from text descriptions for a marketing campaign
Speeding up database queries with optimized indexing
explanation:
Generative AI creates new content, and producing photorealistic images from text descriptions for a marketing campaign is content generation, a classic generative AI use case.
Intrusion detection is a security and classification task. Forecasting stock trends from historical data is predictive analytics. Optimizing database indexing is performance tuning. None of these create new content, so they are not generative AI use cases.

text: While picking a foundation model (FM) on Amazon Bedrock, a research team needs to know how much text it can pack into a single prompt. Which model property tells them this?
explanation:
The context window defines how many tokens a foundation model can take in at once, so it determines how much information fits into a single prompt.
Temperature controls output randomness, not input capacity. Model size relates to parameter count and overall capability, not prompt length. Batch size concerns how many inputs are processed together, not how much text one prompt can hold.

text: A small studio wants to prototype on Amazon Bedrock on a tight budget and avoid any long-term commitment. Which Amazon Bedrock pricing model fits?
explanation:
The On-Demand pricing model charges only for what is used with no upfront or long-term commitment, which fits a limited budget that needs flexibility.
Provisioned Throughput requires committing to and paying for a fixed capacity level over time. Model customization is a fine-tuning activity, not a flexible pricing option. Spot Instances are an Amazon EC2 pricing concept and are not an Amazon Bedrock pricing model.

text: A data-science team wants to stand up a foundation model (FM) quickly inside its own VPC. Which AWS service or feature lets the team do that?
explanation:
Amazon SageMaker JumpStart offers pre-built foundation models that a team can deploy quickly inside its own VPC and begin using right away, which matches the requirement.
Amazon Personalize is a recommendation service, not an FM-deployment feature. PartyRock is a public playground for experimenting with apps, not for deploying FMs in a VPC. Amazon SageMaker AI endpoints host models for inference, but they do not provide a curated catalog of pre-built foundation models ready to deploy with a few clicks, which is the value JumpStart adds.

text: A retail company keeps large volumes of sales data in a database. It wants an application that lets non-technical staff type a plain-language question and have it automatically turned into a SQL query. Which type of model is best suited to power this application?
explanation:
Generative pre-trained transformers are large language models trained to generate text, and they can translate a natural-language request into a structured SQL query, which lets non-technical staff retrieve data without writing SQL themselves, exactly as the requirement describes.
A residual neural network (ResNet) is a deep architecture built for image recognition and computer vision, not language generation. A support vector machine (SVM) is a classic supervised algorithm for classification or regression and cannot generate SQL from text. WaveNet is a generative model for producing realistic audio and speech, so it is the wrong modality for converting text into queries.

text: A company summarizes contracts with an Amazon Bedrock base model and has now trained a custom model for better quality. What must the company do to use the custom model in Amazon Bedrock?
options: Deploy the custom model to an Amazon SageMaker AI endpoint for real-time inference
Register the model in the Amazon SageMaker Model Registry
Request model access for the custom model in Amazon Bedrock
Purchase Provisioned Throughput for the custom model
explanation:
To run a custom (fine-tuned) model in Amazon Bedrock, the company must purchase Provisioned Throughput for that model, which allocates the dedicated capacity Bedrock requires to serve custom models.
Deploying to a SageMaker AI endpoint or registering in the SageMaker Model Registry are Amazon SageMaker workflows, not how Bedrock serves a custom model. Requesting model access applies to Bedrock base models, not to using your own custom model.

text: A company is building an application that must generate synthetic data based on its existing data. Which type of model can the company use to meet this requirement?
explanation:
A generative adversarial network (GAN) is built from two competing neural networks, a generator that creates synthetic samples resembling the real data and a discriminator that tries to tell real from generated, and through this competition it learns to produce realistic synthetic data based on an existing dataset, which is exactly what the company needs.
XGBoost is a gradient-boosting algorithm for supervised classification and regression, not for generating new data. A residual neural network (ResNet) is a deep convolutional architecture used mainly for image recognition and classification. WaveNet is a generative model, but it is specialized for synthesising raw audio such as speech rather than producing general synthetic data from an arbitrary existing dataset.

text: In AI and Natural Language Processing (NLP), what is the term for the numerical representations of real-world objects and concepts that help models better understand text?
explanation:
Embeddings are numerical vector representations of objects and concepts such as words or phrases; by placing similar items close together in vector space they capture relationships and meaning, which helps AI and NLP models understand and work with text more effectively.
Tokens are the individual units, such as words or sub-words, that text is split into before processing, not representations of meaning. A model is the trained system that makes predictions, not a representation of a concept. Parameters are the internal weights a model learns during training and do not represent real-world objects or concepts.

text: A retail analyst wants charts of top-product sales by store over the last year generated automatically. Which AWS solution fits this need?
explanation:
Amazon Q in Amazon QuickSight lets users ask questions in natural language and automatically builds charts and visualizations, such as total sales for top products, which meets the requirement.
Amazon Q Developer assists with coding tasks. Amazon Q in AWS Chatbot helps operate AWS resources from chat channels. Amazon Q in Amazon EC2 provides EC2 guidance. None of these generate business data visualizations.

text: A travel company receives a flood of booking questions every day and plans to use Agents for Amazon Bedrock to keep up. What is a key benefit of using these agents?
options: Generating custom foundation models (FMs) to predict customer needs
Choosing a foundation model (FM) based on predefined criteria and metrics
Automating repetitive tasks and orchestrating complex, multi-step workflows
Calling several foundation models (FMs) at once and merging their results
explanation:
Agents for Amazon Bedrock automate repetitive tasks and orchestrate complex, multi-step workflows, which lets the company handle high volumes of inquiries faster and more efficiently.
Agents do not generate custom foundation models, they do not choose a model by predefined criteria, and their purpose is not to call multiple models and merge results. Their value is task automation and workflow orchestration.

text: A startup is budgeting for a generative AI app on Amazon Bedrock and wants to know what drives the cost of each inference from a large language model (LLM). Which factor is it?
options: The temperature value used for generation
The amount of data used to train the LLM
The total time spent training the LLM
explanation:
Inference cost is driven by the number of tokens consumed, because LLM pricing charges for the input and output tokens processed by each request.
The temperature value only shapes output randomness and has no cost impact. The amount of training data and the total training time affect the one-time cost of building the model, not the cost of running inference.

text: A company customized an Amazon Bedrock foundation model (FM) and now needs to upload a dataset for Bedrock to validate the model's answers. Which AWS service should hold that dataset?
explanation:
Amazon S3 is the scalable object storage service that integrates with Amazon Bedrock, so it is the right place to upload and store the validation dataset for Bedrock to use.
Amazon EBS provides block storage for EC2 volumes, Amazon EFS provides shared file storage for instances, and AWS Snowcone is an edge data-transfer device. None of these is the storage service that Bedrock reads datasets from.

text: A logistics company's analysts have little coding experience but need to build data integration jobs in AWS Glue. Which AWS service can help them?
explanation:
Amazon Q Developer is a generative AI coding assistant that can generate and explain code, helping users with limited programming experience build and work with AWS Glue jobs.
AWS Config tracks resource configuration and compliance. Amazon Personalize provides recommendations. Amazon Comprehend performs NLP tasks such as sentiment and entity analysis. None of these helps write or simplify AWS Glue code.

text: A development team wants a large language model (LLM) to write code from plain-language comments. Which LLM capability does this rely on?
explanation:
Text generation is the LLM capability that produces new text, in this case code, from a given input such as natural-language comments, which is exactly what the requirement needs.
Text summarization condenses existing text. Text classification assigns labels to text. Text completion only continues a given snippet rather than generating full code from descriptive comments.

text: A pharmacy chain wants a short overview of each new medication based on its customer reviews. Which solution meets this requirement?
options: Build a time-series forecasting model to analyze the reviews with Amazon Personalize
Build a classification model that sorts medications into groups with Amazon Comprehend
Generate medication review summaries with Amazon Bedrock large language models (LLMs)
Generate medication review summaries with Amazon Rekognition
explanation:
Amazon Bedrock provides large language models well suited to summarization, so generating concise summaries of medication reviews with Bedrock LLMs meets the requirement.
A time-series forecasting model with Amazon Personalize predicts future values and is not for summarizing text. A classification model with Amazon Comprehend sorts items into categories rather than producing a written overview. Amazon Rekognition analyzes images and video, not text reviews.

text: A developer wants a service that offers foundation models (FMs) for building and scaling generative AI applications. Which AWS service provides this?
explanation:
Amazon Bedrock gives access to foundation models from AWS and third parties through a managed service, so users can build and scale generative AI applications without managing infrastructure.
Amazon Q Developer is a coding assistant. Amazon Kendra is an intelligent enterprise search service. Amazon Comprehend is an NLP service. None of these provides foundation models for building generative AI apps.

text: A subscription box company runs a generative AI support chatbot and wants to measure its financial effect on operations. Which metric should the company track?
options: Cost of training the AI models
explanation:
Cost per customer conversation directly quantifies the operational expense of using the chatbot, so the company can measure its financial effect and compare it to alternatives such as human agents.
The number of inquiries handled measures volume, not cost. Average handle time measures efficiency and speed. The cost of training the models is a one-time build cost, not the ongoing operational cost of conversations.

text: An insurer's support chatbot on Amazon Bedrock needs several turns to resolve a claim. How can the large language model (LLM) use content from the customer's earlier messages?
options: Turn on model invocation logging to collect the messages
Use Amazon Personalize to store the conversation history
Include the previous messages in the model prompt
Use Provisioned Throughput for the LLM
explanation:
Including the previous messages in the model prompt gives the LLM the conversation history it needs, so it can keep context across turns and respond coherently.
Model invocation logging records requests for monitoring but does not feed history back into the model. Amazon Personalize is a recommendation service, not a way to supply prompt context. Provisioned Throughput sets capacity and does not add conversation context.

text: A call-center team manually gives customers location-based product tips and wants foundation models (FMs) to automate it. Which AWS service meets this need?
explanation:
Amazon Bedrock lets the company use foundation models to generate product descriptions and location-based recommendations without managing infrastructure, which automates the task.
Amazon Macie discovers and protects sensitive data. Amazon Textract extracts text from documents. Amazon Transcribe converts speech to text. None of these provides foundation models to generate recommendations.

text: An investment firm uses ML across its operations. Which of these is a generative AI use case?
options: Segmenting customers by type of investment
explanation:
Summarizing customer complaints generates new, condensed text from longer input, which is a generative AI task typically handled by large language models.
Classifying customers by product usage and forecasting revenue are predictive tasks, and segmenting customers by investment type is clustering. These are traditional ML tasks that do not generate new content.

text: Which statement describes a defining characteristic of transformer-based language models?
options: They use convolutional layers to apply filters across the input and capture local patterns
They use self-attention mechanisms to capture contextual relationships
They can process only text data
They process a sequence one element at a time in repeated cycles
explanation:
Transformer-based models use self-attention mechanisms that weigh the importance of each token relative to the others, which lets them capture contextual relationships across an entire input.
Convolutional layers are characteristic of CNNs, not transformers. Transformers are not limited to text and can be multimodal. Processing one element at a time in cycles describes recurrent networks (RNNs), not the parallel self-attention of transformers.

text: A newsroom is piloting a generative AI writing aide. Pilot traffic is light, performance is not a concern, and future usage is unpredictable; the newsroom wants the lowest cost. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: Use Amazon Bedrock with On-Demand pricing
Use Amazon Bedrock with Provisioned Throughput
explanation:
Amazon Bedrock with On-Demand pricing charges only for the inference calls actually made, with no capacity commitment, so it keeps costs low during a small pilot and scales elastically with unpredictable future demand.
GPU-powered EC2 instances incur ongoing costs whether or not they are used. Provisioned Throughput requires paying for committed capacity that low, unpredictable usage would waste. Amazon SageMaker JumpStart still requires provisioning and managing hosting capacity, which is not the most cost-effective for this case.

text: A company fine-tuned a custom large language model (LLM) from Amazon Bedrock and will serve a steady, predictable number of requests per minute in production. Which option is MOST cost-effective?
options: Deploy the model on an Amazon EC2 compute optimized instance
Purchase Provisioned Throughput for the model on Amazon Bedrock
Use the model with On-Demand throughput on Amazon Bedrock
Store the model in Amazon S3 and host it with AWS Lambda
explanation:
For steady, predictable request volume, Provisioned Throughput on Amazon Bedrock offers a lower per-request cost by committing to a fixed throughput level, making it the most cost-effective way to serve a custom model.
An EC2 compute optimized instance means self-managing infrastructure and is not how Bedrock serves custom models. On-Demand throughput costs more per request at steady high volume. Storing the model in Amazon S3 and hosting it with AWS Lambda is not a supported way to serve a Bedrock custom model.

text: A medical clinic wants a generative AI tool with speech-to-text that helps doctors dictate and create clinical notes. Which AWS service meets this requirement?
explanation:
AWS HealthScribe is purpose-built for healthcare and combines speech recognition with generative AI to transcribe clinical conversations and produce structured clinical notes, which meets the clinic's need.
Amazon Q Developer is a coding assistant. Amazon Polly performs text-to-speech, the opposite direction. Amazon Rekognition analyzes images and video, not clinical speech.

text: In a large language model (LLM), what do vector embeddings make possible?
options: Splitting text into manageable pieces of data
Grouping a set of characters to be treated as a single unit
Counting every word in the input
explanation:
Vector embeddings convert text into numerical vectors that capture meaning, so texts can be compared mathematically by measuring distance or similarity, which supports tasks like retrieval and clustering.
Splitting text into manageable pieces describes chunking. Grouping characters into a single unit describes tokenization. Counting every word is a simple word-frequency count, not an embedding.

text: An edtech company is building an app where students type a question or snap a photo of one, and the app returns a written answer with an explanation. Which type of model should power the app?
explanation:
A large multimodal language model can take both text and images as input and generate text output, so it can accept a typed or photographed question and return a written answer with an explanation.
A Computer Vision model analyzes images but does not generate explanatory text answers. A diffusion model generates images, not text answers. A text-to-speech model converts text into audio, which does not produce written answers from mixed inputs.

text: Which statement correctly describes embeddings in generative AI?
options: Embeddings search data to find the most helpful information for answering natural-language questions
Embeddings lower hardware requirements by using a less precise data type for weights and activations
Embeddings represent data as high-dimensional vectors that capture semantic relationships
Embeddings store and retrieve data for generative AI applications
explanation:
Embeddings map inputs such as words or documents into high-dimensional vectors where semantic similarity corresponds to closeness in the vector space, letting models reason about meaning and relationships.
Searching data to find helpful information describes retrieval, as in RAG. Reducing hardware needs with a less precise data type describes quantization. Storing and retrieving data describes a database or vector store, not embeddings themselves.

text: A company needs a generative AI model for an app that must answer users in real time. Which model characteristic matters most?
explanation:
Inference speed determines how quickly the model generates a response, so it is the key characteristic for a real-time application where users need answers with low latency.
Model complexity affects capability and cost but not directly the real-time requirement. Training time is a one-time build concern. Innovation speed describes how fast a model family evolves, none of which governs real-time response latency.

text: What is the term for the instructions you give a foundation model (FM) to help it return a more accurate answer?
explanation:
A prompt is the input instruction or query provided to a foundation model that guides what it should do, helping it produce a more accurate response.
Direction and dialog are not the term for the model's input instruction. Translation is a task type, not the instruction itself.

text: A company wants an AI assistant that lets employees ask questions about internal company data. Which AWS service meets this need?
explanation:
Amazon Q Business builds generative AI assistants that connect to internal data sources, so employees can ask questions and get answers, which meets the requirement.
Amazon Rekognition analyzes images and video. Amazon Textract extracts text from documents. Amazon Lex builds conversational chatbots but is not designed as an enterprise assistant over internal company data.

text: A team wants a low-cost, hands-on way to experiment with and learn about generative AI applications. Which solution is MOST cost-effective?
explanation:
Amazon Bedrock PartyRock provides a low-cost, hands-on playground for building and experimenting with generative AI applications, which fits learning in an experimental environment cost-effectively.
Amazon Q Developer is a coding assistant. Amazon SageMaker JumpStart requires provisioning and managing model hosting. Amazon Q Business is an enterprise assistant over company data. None of these is a low-cost experimentation playground for learning about generative AI apps.

text: A studio that produces video content wants to use generative AI to create new clips and cut production time. Which solution meets these requirements MOST operationally efficiently?
options: Use the Amazon Titan Image Generator model on Amazon Bedrock to create intermediate images, then assemble videos with video editing software
Use the Amazon Nova Reel model on Amazon Bedrock to generate videos
Use the Amazon Nova Canvas model on Amazon Bedrock to create intermediate images, then assemble videos with video editing software
Use the Amazon Nova Pro model on Amazon Bedrock to generate videos
explanation:
The Amazon Nova Reel model on Amazon Bedrock is built for generative video creation, so it lets the company generate new video content directly and reduce production time in the most operationally efficient way.
Using Amazon Titan Image Generator or Amazon Nova Canvas produces only still images that then require manual editing into videos, which adds steps. Amazon Nova Pro is a general multimodal model and is not the purpose-built video-generation option.

text: A compliance team wants to pull the key insights out of long policy documents so staff can work faster. Which generative AI strategy meets this requirement?
explanation:
Summarization condenses large documents into their key insights, so employees can quickly grasp and act on the essential information.
Regression predicts numeric values, clustering groups similar items, and classification assigns labels. None of these extracts and condenses the key insights from a document.

text: An online store uses a generative AI assistant on Amazon Bedrock to recommend products and wants to measure its direct impact on sales. Which metric meets this requirement?
options: The number of customer interactions with the AI assistant
Sentiment analysis scores from customer feedback after interactions
The conversion rate of customers who purchase after interacting with the AI assistant
explanation:
Conversion rate, the share of customers who buy after interacting with the assistant, ties assistant engagement directly to sales outcomes, so it measures the direct impact on sales.
The number of interactions measures usage volume, not sales. Sentiment scores measure customer mood. Natural language understanding accuracy measures technical quality. None of these directly measures sales impact.

text: Which scenario is a practical use case for generative AI?
options: Using an ML model to forecast product demand
Tracking website traffic and user behavior with an analytics dashboard
Using a chatbot to give human-like responses to customer queries in real time
Using a rule-based recommendation engine to suggest products
explanation:
A chatbot that gives human-like responses to customer queries in real time uses a generative model to create relevant, natural-language answers, which is a practical generative AI use case.
Forecasting product demand with an ML model is predictive analytics. An analytics dashboard tracks metrics. A rule-based recommendation engine follows fixed rules. None of these generates new content.

text: What is the difference between discriminative and generative AI models?
options: Discriminative models are faster than generative models
Discriminative models are more accurate than generative models
Discriminative models classify or predict, while generative models create new content
Discriminative models need more data than generative models
explanation:
Discriminative models learn to classify inputs or predict outcomes, whereas generative models learn to create new content similar to their training data; this is the core distinction between the two.
Claims that discriminative models are inherently faster, more accurate, or need more data are not the defining difference and are not generally true; the real distinction is what each type of model produces.

text: What is the primary purpose of Amazon Q Business?
options: To provide AI-powered business assistance over company data
explanation:
Amazon Q Business is a generative AI assistant for the enterprise; its primary purpose is to provide AI-powered assistance over a company's internal data, answering questions, generating content, and summarizing information while respecting access controls.
Training custom ML models is the role of Amazon SageMaker AI. Storing large datasets is the role of services like Amazon S3. Monitoring infrastructure is the role of services like Amazon CloudWatch. None of these is the purpose of Amazon Q Business.

text: A company is comparing Amazon Nova models on Amazon Bedrock and needs a multimodal model that supports several languages. Which Nova model meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
explanation:
Amazon Nova Lite is a low-cost multimodal model that supports multiple languages, so it meets the multimodal and multilingual requirements as the most cost-effective Nova option.
Amazon Nova Pro is also multimodal but is a higher-cost, higher-capability model. Amazon Nova Canvas generates images and Amazon Nova Reel generates video, so these single-purpose generation models are not cost-effective multilingual multimodal choices.

text: An edtech company is building a reading app that lets students add illustrations to their stories. Which solution meets this requirement?
options: Use Amazon Polly to create an audiobook from the story text
Use Amazon Rekognition to analyze image content and detect text attributes
Use Amazon Bedrock Stable Diffusion 3.5 Large to generate images from text inputs
Create a standard prompt template and use Amazon Q Business to illustrate the stories
explanation:
Amazon Bedrock Stable Diffusion 3.5 Large generates images from text prompts, so students can create illustrations for their stories from descriptions, which supports reading comprehension with visuals.
Amazon Polly converts text to speech, producing audio rather than illustrations. Amazon Rekognition analyzes existing images rather than generating new ones. Amazon Q Business is an enterprise assistant over company data and does not generate story illustrations.

text: A developer wants to quickly create a test case and documentation for some code with the LEAST effort. Which solution meets this requirement?
options: Upload the code to an online coding assistant
Use Amazon Q Developer in an integrated development environment (IDE)
Build an application that uses foundation models (FMs)
Research and write the test cases by hand, then add the documentation
explanation:
Amazon Q Developer in an IDE can automatically generate test cases and documentation for code, which meets the requirement with the least effort.
Uploading code to an online coding assistant adds manual steps and data-handling concerns. Building a custom application on foundation models is far more effort. Researching and writing everything by hand is the most effort of all.

text: An ecommerce company needs to generate thousands of unique product descriptions a day, written as paragraphs with a consistent style and tone. Which type of generative model meets these requirements?
explanation:
Transformer-based models, such as large language models, generate coherent paragraphs of text with consistent style and tone and scale to producing thousands of unique descriptions, which fits the requirement.
Variational autoencoders and generative adversarial networks are used mainly to generate images or other data, not fluent long-form text. Diffusion models generate images, so none of these is suited to producing styled product-description text at scale.

text: What is a token in the context of generative AI?
options: A unit of text processed by the model
explanation:
A token is the basic unit of text, such as a word or sub-word, that a model processes and generates, which is what the term refers to.
A token is not a security feature, not a type of neural network, and not a model evaluation metric; those describe unrelated concepts.

text: What is a primary advantage of the adaptability of generative AI?
options: It can work only with structured data
It can handle a wide range of tasks and domains
It removes the need for any human oversight
explanation:
Adaptability means a generative model can be applied to a wide range of tasks and domains, which is its key advantage.
Generative AI is not limited to structured data, it does not always produce perfect results, and it does not remove the need for human oversight; these claims misstate its capabilities.

text: Which AWS service is designed specifically for developing generative AI applications?
explanation:
Amazon Bedrock is purpose-built for generative AI, providing access to foundation models and tools to build and scale generative AI applications.
Amazon EC2 provides general compute, Amazon S3 provides object storage, and Amazon RDS provides managed relational databases; none is specifically designed for developing generative AI applications.

text: What is a foundation model in generative AI?
options: A model that can only generate text
A model designed specifically for image generation
A large, pre-trained model that can be adapted for many tasks
A model that requires no training data
explanation:
A foundation model is a large model pre-trained on vast amounts of data that can be adapted or fine-tuned for many downstream tasks such as text generation, summarization, and question answering.
A foundation model is not limited to text and is not built only for image generation, and it is trained on large amounts of data, so the claim that it needs no training data is incorrect.

text: What is a primary advantage of using AWS generative AI services to build applications?
options: They lower the barrier to entry
They remove the need for any coding
explanation:
AWS generative AI services provide managed infrastructure, pre-trained foundation models, and APIs, which lower the barrier to entry by removing the need to build and train large models from scratch.
These services are not always free, they do not guarantee perfect accuracy, and they do not remove the need for any coding; those statements overstate what the services provide.

text: In generative AI, what are tokens?
options: The vector representations of words or concepts
The basic units of input and output, such as words or subwords
The instructions or prompts given to the model
The hidden layers of the neural network
explanation:
Tokens are the smallest units, such as words, subwords, or characters, that a generative model reads and produces, forming the basis of its input and output.
Vector representations describe embeddings, prompts are the instructions given to the model, and hidden layers are part of the model's architecture; none of these defines a token.

text: Which two statements about a model's latent space are correct?
options: It must be stored in a specific type of database
It captures the model's internal understanding of relationships among concepts
It applies only to image data
It enables computing semantic similarity between different inputs
It is a human-readable lookup table
explanation:
A model's latent space is the internal representation where it organizes concepts, so it both captures the relationships the model has learned and lets it compute semantic similarity between different inputs.
Latent space is not limited to images, does not require a specific database type, and is not a human-readable lookup table.

text: In the generative AI model lifecycle, which stage runs tests to check the model's accuracy?
explanation:
The evaluation stage tests the model against validation or hold-out data using metrics such as accuracy before it moves to deployment.
Pre-training builds the base model, fine-tuning adapts it to a task, and deployment puts the finished model into production; none of these is where accuracy testing happens.

text: What is the primary benefit of Amazon SageMaker JumpStart?
options: It provides access to pre-trained models and solutions
It manages data labeling with a human workforce
explanation:
Amazon SageMaker JumpStart provides access to pre-trained models, built-in algorithms, and end-to-end solutions, which speeds up the start of machine learning and generative AI projects.
Reducing inference cost, hyperparameter tuning, and managed human labeling are handled by other capabilities, such as SageMaker Automatic Model Tuning and SageMaker Ground Truth Plus.

text: Which of the following is NOT a stage of the foundation model (FM) lifecycle?
explanation:
Marketing is a business activity and is not part of the technical FM lifecycle, which covers stages such as data selection, pre-training, fine-tuning, evaluation, and deployment.
Fine-tuning, pre-training, and deployment are all genuine lifecycle stages, so none of them is the correct answer to what is NOT a stage.

text: In generative AI, what is prompt engineering?
options: A method for compressing models to run faster
The process of crafting effective input prompts to guide a model's outputs
A technique for designing a model's neural network architecture
The process of labeling training data for supervised learning
explanation:
Prompt engineering is the practice of designing and refining input prompts, for example by adding context, constraints, or examples, to guide a generative model toward accurate, relevant outputs.
It is not model compression, not the design of a neural network architecture, and not the labeling of training data.

text: An AI practitioner uses a large language model to write marketing copy. The output sounds plausible and factual but is actually incorrect. Which problem is the model exhibiting?
explanation:
Hallucination is when a large language model produces content that sounds plausible and factual but is actually incorrect or fabricated, which matches the marketing copy described.
Data leakage is the unintended exposure of information, overfitting is when a model memorizes training data and generalizes poorly, and underfitting is when a model is too simple to capture patterns. None of these describes confidently stated but false output.

text: A company has an application that ingests consumer complaints from public sources and processes them with complex hard-coded rules. The company wants to scale this logic across new markets and product lines. Which advantage of generative AI models applies to this scenario?
explanation:
Adaptability is the generative AI advantage that applies here: the models can generalize learned patterns to new markets and product lines with little manual reconfiguration, avoiding the need to rewrite complex hard-coded rules.
Predictable outputs and reduced sensitivity to input changes are not strengths of generative AI, which is nondeterministic and sensitive to input wording. Explainability is unrelated to scaling the complaint-processing logic.

text: An AI practitioner notices that a large language model returns different responses each time it receives the same input. Which risk of AI does this describe?
explanation:
Nondeterminism is the property by which a large language model can return different responses to the same input because of randomness in how it generates text, which matches the observed behavior.
Hallucinations are fabricated but plausible outputs, accuracy concerns correctness, and multimodality is the ability to work across data types such as text and images. None of these describes varying responses to identical inputs.

text: In the context of generative AI, what is a hallucination?
options: A visual output produced by the model
An incorrect or fabricated output presented as fact
A method of training a model
explanation:
A hallucination is an output that is incorrect or fabricated but is presented by the model as if it were factual.
A hallucination is not a visual output, a type of model architecture, or a method of training a model. These options describe unrelated concepts.

text: Which of the following is a potential disadvantage of generative AI solutions?
explanation:
Inaccuracy is a known disadvantage of generative AI, which can produce incorrect, biased, or fabricated information that requires validation and human oversight.
Adaptability and responsiveness are advantages of generative AI, and simplicity is not a disadvantage. None of these represents a drawback of generative AI solutions.

text: A media company wants to use an AWS-developed foundation model to generate marketing copy and images. Which AWS service provides first-party foundation models built by Amazon?
explanation:
Amazon Nova is a family of foundation models developed by AWS that can generate text, images, and other content, making it the appropriate choice when a company wants to use first-party Amazon-built foundation models for content generation.
Amazon Rekognition analyzes images and video for object detection and facial recognition but does not generate content. Amazon Comprehend extracts insights such as sentiment and entities from text. Amazon Polly converts text to speech. None of these is a generative foundation model built by Amazon.

text: A development team is building a customer support assistant on Amazon Bedrock. The assistant must remember account details from earlier in the conversation, reference relevant help articles, and follow company guidelines. Which concept describes managing all of this information that is fed to the foundation model?
explanation:
Context engineering is the practice of managing the full set of information provided to a foundation model at inference time, including conversation history, retrieved documents, system instructions, and any other relevant data, so the model produces accurate, grounded responses that account for all necessary context.
Prompt engineering focuses specifically on crafting the instruction or query text itself, whereas context engineering encompasses the broader strategy of assembling all relevant information the model needs. Model distillation compresses a larger model into a smaller one for efficiency. Continuous pre-training updates a model's knowledge by training on new data over time, not by managing runtime context.

text: A legal firm's AI assistant on Amazon Bedrock must combine the user's question, relevant contract clauses retrieved from a knowledge base, the firm's compliance rules, and the conversation history into a single model call. Which practice governs how these elements are assembled and prioritized?
explanation:
Context engineering governs how all the information elements, such as retrieved documents, system rules, user input, and conversation history, are assembled, prioritized, and structured before being passed to the model, ensuring it has the right context to answer accurately.
Fine-tuning updates model weights with new training data and does not control what is passed at inference time. Hyperparameter tuning adjusts training configuration settings like learning rate and batch size. Feature engineering transforms raw data into model inputs during the ML training pipeline, not at inference time for a foundation model.

text: What is the role of Model Context Protocol (MCP) in agentic AI systems?
options: It compresses models to reduce inference latency
It provides a standard interface for connecting AI agents to external tools and data sources
It encrypts model weights during training
It measures model accuracy on benchmark datasets
explanation:
Model Context Protocol (MCP) provides a standardized interface that allows AI agents to connect to external tools, APIs, and data sources in a consistent way, enabling them to retrieve information and take actions across different systems without custom integrations for each one.
