Model compression for reduced latency describes techniques like quantization or distillation. Encrypting model weights is a security practice handled by services like AWS KMS. Measuring accuracy on benchmarks is model evaluation. None of these describes a protocol for agent-to-tool connectivity.

text: A financial services company wants multiple specialized AI agents to collaborate on complex customer requests. One agent handles account queries, another processes transactions, and a third checks compliance. Which agentic AI concept does this architecture represent?
explanation:
A multi-agent system pattern uses multiple specialized AI agents that communicate and collaborate to handle complex tasks, with each agent responsible for a specific capability such as account queries, transactions, or compliance checks, which matches the architecture described.
Single-agent reinforcement learning trains one agent through environmental rewards without collaboration between multiple agents. A supervised classification pipeline assigns labels to inputs and does not involve agent collaboration. A batch inference workflow processes data in bulk offline and has no concept of multiple agents working together.

text: An AI agent assists a healthcare researcher over multiple sessions spanning several days. The agent needs to recall findings from previous sessions to avoid repeating work. Which agentic AI capability enables this?
explanation:
Memory management in agentic AI allows an agent to persist and retrieve information across sessions, so it can recall previous findings, avoid redundant work, and build on past interactions over time.
Tool usage enables agents to call external APIs and services but does not handle storing and retrieving past interaction history. Workflow orchestration coordinates the sequence of steps an agent takes but does not address long-term memory. Model pre-training builds the base model's knowledge during initial training, not the ability to remember individual user sessions.

text: A startup wants to build custom AI agents using an open-source Python SDK that supports tool use, multi-agent orchestration, and integration with multiple model providers. Which AWS service meets this requirement?
explanation:
Strands Agents is an open-source Python SDK from AWS that lets developers build AI agents with tool use, multi-agent orchestration, and flexibility to work with different model providers, which matches what the startup needs.
Amazon Personalize generates recommendations from user behavior data. Amazon Comprehend performs Natural Language Processing tasks like sentiment analysis. Amazon Lex builds conversational chatbots and voice interfaces. None of these provides an open-source SDK for building custom AI agents with multi-agent orchestration.

text: An enterprise wants managed infrastructure to deploy, scale, and monitor its AI agents in production without handling the underlying compute and networking. Which AWS service meets this requirement?
explanation:
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore provides managed infrastructure for deploying, scaling, and monitoring AI agents in production, handling the compute, networking, and operational concerns so the enterprise can focus on agent logic rather than infrastructure management.
Amazon SageMaker Canvas is a no-code interface for building ML models. Amazon Kendra provides intelligent enterprise search. Amazon Polly converts text to speech. None of these provides managed infrastructure specifically for running AI agents in production.

text: A travel agency builds an AI agent that can search flight availability, book tickets, and process payments by calling the airline's APIs. Which agentic AI capability allows the agent to interact with these external systems?
explanation:
Tool usage is the agentic AI capability that allows an agent to call external APIs, services, and systems to retrieve information or take actions, which is how the travel agent searches flights, books tickets, and processes payments through the airline's APIs.
Memory management stores and retrieves information across interactions but does not call external systems. Model fine-tuning updates model weights during training rather than enabling runtime API calls. Prompt caching stores frequently used prompts for efficiency but does not interact with external systems.

text: A company uses Amazon Bedrock for a customer support chatbot and notices costs increasing. The team discovers that full conversation histories are included in every prompt. Which aspect of the token-based pricing model explains this?
options: Cost is based on the number of API calls regardless of content
Cost increases with the total number of input and output tokens processed per request
Cost is determined by the time the model spends processing each request
Cost depends on the number of concurrent users
explanation:
Token-based pricing charges for the total number of input and output tokens processed in each request, so including long conversation histories increases the input token count on every call and directly drives up costs.
Amazon Bedrock does not charge a flat fee per API call regardless of content. Pricing is not based on processing time or concurrent user count; it is based on token volume.

text: How does reducing the maximum output token limit affect cost and performance when using a foundation model?
options: It increases cost but has no effect on response time
It decreases cost and can reduce response time
It has no effect on cost or response time
It increases response time but decreases cost
explanation:
Reducing the maximum output token limit means fewer tokens are generated per request, which directly lowers cost under token-based pricing and can also reduce response time because the model produces less output.
Fewer output tokens means less to pay for, so cost does not increase. Output tokens directly affect both billing and generation time, so there is an effect. Generating fewer tokens is faster, not slower.

text: A startup with no ML infrastructure wants to launch a generative AI feature quickly. Which advantage of using AWS GenAI services like Amazon Bedrock is most relevant?
options: The startup must train its own foundation model from scratch
AWS GenAI services lower the barrier to entry by providing managed access to pre-trained foundation models
AWS GenAI services require the startup to manage GPU clusters
AWS GenAI services are only available to enterprise customers
explanation:
AWS GenAI services like Amazon Bedrock provide managed access to pre-trained foundation models through APIs, which lowers the barrier to entry by removing the need to train models, manage infrastructure, or procure GPUs, letting the startup launch quickly.
The startup does not need to train its own model because pre-trained models are available. AWS manages the infrastructure so the startup does not manage GPU clusters. These services are available to all customers, not only enterprises.

text: A healthcare company is evaluating whether to build its generative AI application on AWS. Which benefit of AWS infrastructure is most important for this regulated industry?
options: AWS provides the lowest possible inference latency globally
AWS infrastructure provides built-in security, compliance certifications, and data protection controls
AWS guarantees that AI models never produce incorrect outputs
AWS eliminates the need for any data governance policies
explanation:
AWS infrastructure provides security controls, compliance certifications (such as HIPAA eligibility), and data protection features that regulated industries like healthcare require to deploy AI applications responsibly and meet legal obligations.
No provider guarantees the lowest latency globally in all cases. No AI system can guarantee it never produces incorrect outputs. AWS does not eliminate the need for data governance; organizations must still implement their own policies.

text: A retail company deployed a generative AI chatbot six months ago and wants to measure its business value. Which metric best indicates the chatbot's impact on revenue?
explanation:
Average revenue per user measures the financial value generated from each customer, so tracking whether it increases after deploying the chatbot directly indicates the chatbot's revenue impact.
Model parameter count describes model size. Number of training epochs is a training configuration detail. Inference latency measures response speed. None of these reflects revenue impact.

text: A company uses a generative AI assistant to help its support team and wants to measure operational efficiency gains. Which metric should it track?
options: Efficiency measured as reduction in average handle time per case
explanation:
Reduction in average handle time per case directly measures how much faster agents resolve issues with the AI assistant's help, which is an operational efficiency gain and a business value metric for GenAI applications.
ROUGE and BERTScore measure generated text quality against references. Model perplexity measures language-modeling fit. None of these captures operational efficiency.

text: Which stage of the foundation model lifecycle involves selecting the right data sources and preparing them before any model training begins?
explanation:
Data selection is the first stage of the foundation model lifecycle, where appropriate data sources are identified and curated before pre-training begins. The quality and breadth of selected data directly shapes what the model learns.
Deployment is a later stage where the trained model is made available for inference. Evaluation assesses model performance after training. Feedback is the final stage where user interactions inform improvements.

text: A company invested in a generative AI solution to automate report writing. Which metric best measures whether this investment delivered financial value?
explanation:
Return on investment (ROI) measures whether the financial benefits of the AI solution, such as labor savings and faster output, exceed the costs of building and running it, which directly shows whether the investment delivered financial value.
Model accuracy measures prediction quality but not financial return. Number of parameters and training data volume are technical details unrelated to business value.

text: A travel company uses a pre-trained large language model (LLM) to power a booking assistant. The company needs the assistant's replies to be brief and written in a particular language. Which approach will best align the LLM's output with these expectations?
options: Choose an LLM of a different size
explanation:
Refining the prompt lets the company state the required response length and target language directly, so the model returns brief replies in the chosen language.
Choosing a different model size changes the model's capacity and cost rather than enforcing length or language. Increasing the temperature adds randomness, making the output less controlled. Increasing the Top K value widens the pool of candidate tokens, which also does not control response length or language.

text: A manufacturer needs a high-accuracy labeled image dataset for a defect-detection model and wants to keep mislabeled examples to a minimum. Which approach best meets these requirements?
options: Automated annotation with Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels
Human-in-the-loop validation with Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth Plus
Synthetic image generation with an Amazon Bedrock foundation model
Automated active-learning labeling with Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth
explanation:
Human-in-the-loop validation with Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth Plus routes labels through expert reviewers who verify and correct them, producing the highest-accuracy annotations with the fewest mistakes.
Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels automates labeling but, without human review, can propagate errors; generating synthetic images with an Amazon Bedrock model creates data yet does nothing to validate the labels; SageMaker Ground Truth's automated active-learning labeling cuts effort but raises the chance of incorrect annotations, the opposite of the goal.

text: A company uses a foundation model (FM) from Amazon Bedrock for a search tool. The company wants to fine-tune the FM on its own data to make the tool more accurate. Which approach will correctly fine-tune the model?
options: Purchase Provisioned Throughput for Amazon Bedrock
Supply labeled examples that each contain a prompt field and a completion field
Prepare the dataset as a .txt file that holds multiple lines of .csv content
Train the model on journals and textbooks
explanation:
Fine-tuning a model on Amazon Bedrock requires a labeled dataset in which each record pairs an input prompt with the expected completion, so the model learns the desired input-to-output behavior from the company data.
Provisioned Throughput is a capacity and pricing option for inference, not a fine-tuning method. A .txt file containing .csv lines is not the required fine-tuning format. Training on journals and textbooks is unstructured content that lacks the prompt-and-completion pairs that fine-tuning needs.

text: An engineering team wants to use Amazon OpenSearch Service as the backbone of a vector search application. Which capability makes this possible?
options: k-NN nearest neighbor search over high-dimensional vectors
explanation:
k-NN nearest neighbor search lets Amazon OpenSearch Service index embeddings and return the vectors most similar to a query, which is the core of a vector database application such as semantic search.
BM25 full-text search matches keywords rather than semantic vectors; geospatial indexing handles location data; cross-cluster replication supports availability and disaster recovery. None provides vector similarity search.

text: A company is building a self-service support chatbot on a foundation model (FM). The chatbot's responses must match the company's brand tone. Which solution meets this requirement?
options: Iterate on and refine the prompt until the FM produces responses in the desired style
Set a low limit on the number of tokens the FM can produce
Use batch inference to generate detailed responses
explanation:
Iteratively refining the prompt steers the foundation model toward responses that match the company brand tone, because the prompt instructions and examples shape the style of the output.
Limiting output tokens only shortens responses. Batch inference changes how requests are processed, not their tone. Raising the temperature increases randomness, which makes tone less consistent rather than more aligned.

text: A company wants to use a large language model (LLM) on Amazon Bedrock to label text passages as positive or negative. Which prompt engineering strategy meets this requirement?
options: Add a detailed explanation of sentiment analysis and how LLMs work to the prompt
Provide only the new passage to classify, with no examples or additional context
Include a few example passages, each labeled positive or negative, in the prompt
Include the new passage along with a few examples of unrelated tasks such as summarization or translation
explanation:
Including a few example passages, each labeled positive or negative, is few-shot prompting, which shows the model the input-to-label pattern and improves classification accuracy on a new passage.
Adding an explanation of how sentiment analysis or LLMs work provides theory but no examples to learn from. Providing only the passage with no examples is zero-shot and gives the model less guidance. Examples of unrelated tasks such as summarization or translation steer the model away from sentiment classification.

text: A startup is launching an LLM-powered virtual agent and wants to stop users from coaxing it into unsafe actions or leaking its hidden instructions. Which action most directly reduces this risk?
options: Increase the model's temperature so responses vary more
Raise the Top P value to widen token sampling
Add system instructions in a prompt template that teach the model to recognize and refuse manipulation attempts
Reduce the maximum output length on each request
explanation:
A prompt template with system instructions that teach the model to spot and refuse manipulation patterns is a prompt-engineering safeguard that directly lowers the risk of prompt injection and instruction leakage.
Raising temperature or Top P only changes how random the sampling is, and shortening the maximum output length just truncates responses; none of these counters prompt manipulation.

text: A logistics company runs an Amazon Titan model on Amazon Bedrock and wants the model's answers to draw on its internal shipping documents. Which solution adds this private context?
options: Fine-tune the FM on the internal documents
Create an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base over the internal documents
Switch to a larger foundation model
explanation:
An Amazon Bedrock knowledge base indexes the internal documents and retrieves the relevant passages at query time (RAG), so the Titan model grounds its answers in the company's private data without any training.
Fine-tuning can embed knowledge but is costlier and static, so it is not the targeted way to supplement answers with frequently used documents; lowering the temperature only reduces randomness; switching to a larger model adds capability but still gives it no access to the private documents.

text: An appliance maker wants a chat interface over its PDF product manuals using large language models (LLMs) on Amazon Bedrock, at the lowest cost. Which approach fits best?
options: Add all the manuals to every prompt as context
Upload the manuals to an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base and retrieve only the relevant passages per query
Fine-tune a model on the manuals and serve the fine-tuned model
Continuously pre-train the base model on the manual content
explanation:
A knowledge base retrieves just the passages relevant to each question, so the model gets the right context cheaply, without paying to send whole manuals every time or to train the model.
Pasting all manuals into every prompt inflates token costs; fine-tuning adds training cost and must be redone when manuals change; continuous pre-training on the corpus is the most expensive option and unnecessary for a Q&A interface.

text: A biotech firm's chatbot answers questions from dense clinical research papers, but even after several prompt tweaks the model handles the specialized terminology poorly. What will best improve it?
options: Use few-shot prompting with sample question-and-answer pairs
Apply domain adaptation fine-tuning on the specialized corpus
Add a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) step over the papers
Lower the temperature to make answers more focused
explanation:
Domain adaptation fine-tuning trains the model on the specialized corpus so it actually learns the clinical terminology, which is what fixes poor comprehension of dense domain language.
Few-shot prompting and a lower temperature shape responses but do not teach new vocabulary; a RAG step retrieves relevant passages, yet the model still struggles to interpret the specialized terms it has not learned.

text: An online learning company runs a question-answering assistant and wants the answer style to match each learner's age range, which the app already passes to the model. Which approach needs the LEAST effort?
options: Train a separate fine-tuned model for each age range
Build a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline of age-specific content
Post-process every response with a second model to adjust the tone
Add a role and audience instruction to the prompt that states the user's age range
explanation:
Adding a role and audience instruction to the prompt is a simple prompt-engineering change that steers the style to the stated age range with almost no extra work.
Fine-tuning a model per age range, building a RAG pipeline of age-specific content, and running a second model to rewrite tone all add significant data, infrastructure, or processing effort.

text: A team sends a daily few-shot prompt with 10 examples to a base model on Amazon Bedrock. The model performs well, but the team wants to cut the monthly cost. Which change helps?
options: Purchase Provisioned Throughput for the model
Reduce the number of examples and tokens in the prompt
Fine-tune the model so the examples are no longer needed in the prompt
Move the workload to a larger, more capable model
explanation:
Because cost scales with the tokens processed, trimming the number of examples and tokens in the prompt lowers the bill while the model keeps performing well.
Provisioned Throughput is meant for high, steady volume and would cost more for a once-a-day job; fine-tuning removes in-prompt examples but adds training cost; moving to a larger model increases the per-call cost.

text: A travel company localizes its help articles into several languages with an LLM and scores each machine translation against a human reference. Which metric is purpose-built for machine translation?
explanation:
BLEU is designed for machine translation, measuring n-gram overlap between the candidate translation and one or more human references, which is exactly the comparison described.
ROUGE targets summarization recall; BERTScore measures general semantic similarity rather than serving as the standard translation metric; word error rate evaluates speech transcription.

text: What is a benefit of continuously pre-training a foundation model (FM)?
options: It adapts the model to a specific labeled task dataset
It keeps improving the model's knowledge by training it further on new data over time
It compresses the model to shrink its size and speed up inference
It removes the need for an evaluation step
explanation:
Continuous pre-training keeps exposing the FM to fresh, mostly unlabeled data, so its knowledge stays current and its performance improves over time.
Adapting to a labeled task dataset describes fine-tuning; shrinking and speeding up the model describes distillation or quantization; and no training method removes the need to evaluate the model.

text: Which prompt-based attack is specifically aimed at revealing a model's hidden system instructions?
explanation:
Extracting (leaking) the prompt template coaxes the model into disclosing its underlying system prompt, directly exposing the hidden instructions that configure its behavior.
Jailbreaking bypasses safety controls, prompt injection inserts adversarial instructions to hijack behavior, and persona switching pushes the model into a different role; none of these is aimed at dumping the system instructions themselves.

text: A social platform wants to compare the output toxicity of several candidate LLMs from Amazon SageMaker JumpStart with the LEAST operational effort. Which evaluation approach fits?
options: Model evaluation with a human review workforce
Automatic model evaluation using built-in toxicity metrics
A/B testing the models with live users
explanation:
Automatic model evaluation scores outputs with built-in toxicity metrics and needs no people to recruit or coordinate, giving the lowest operational effort.
Human-workforce evaluation and crowd-sourced rating both require managing reviewers, and A/B testing with live users adds exposure risk and coordination overhead.

text: Which prompting approach is used to harden a model against prompt injection attacks?
explanation:
Adversarial prompting deliberately crafts and tests hostile inputs so injection attempts can be detected and neutralized, hardening the model against them.
Chain-of-thought, few-shot, and zero-shot prompting shape how the model reasons or learns from examples but offer no defense against malicious prompts.

text: An IT support team fine-tuned an LLM to answer help desk questions and wants to confirm the fine-tuning improved its accuracy. Which metric should it use?
explanation:
The F1 score balances precision and recall in one number, so it reflects how accurately and completely the model answers, making it the right way to measure the fine-tuning gain.
Precision alone ignores missed correct answers; time to first token measures latency; perplexity measures language-modeling fit rather than task accuracy.

text: A company uses Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) with Amazon Bedrock and Stable Diffusion to create product images, but the results are random and miss requested details. The team wants the images to follow the prompts more closely. Which change helps?
options: Increase the number of generation steps
explanation:
The CFG scale controls how strongly the model follows the text prompt, so raising it makes the generated image adhere more closely to the requested details.
More generation steps mainly refine denoising quality; a fixed seed only makes results reproducible; increasing the negative prompt weight strengthens what to avoid rather than how closely the image matches the main prompt.

text: A telecom company wants an LLM chatbot that gives support agents real-time answers grounded in internal policy documents, at the lowest cost. Which approach fits best?
options: Fine-tune the LLM on the policy documents
Implement Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) over the policy documents
Pre-train a new model from scratch on the policy corpus
Paste all policy documents into every prompt as context
explanation:
RAG retrieves the relevant policy passages at query time and grounds the chatbot's answers in them, delivering accurate responses cheaply with no training.
Fine-tuning adds training cost and must be repeated as policies change; pre-training from scratch is by far the most expensive option; pasting all documents into every prompt drives up token costs.

text: A company built a text summarization solution on Amazon Bedrock and will use Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation. Which metric should it use to measure summary quality?
explanation:
BERTScore compares the generated summary with reference text using contextual embeddings, capturing semantic similarity, which makes it suitable for measuring summarization quality.
AUC measures binary classification ranking, MSE measures regression error, and perplexity measures language-modeling fit; none of these compares a summary against references for quality.

text: A language-learning app calls an LLM to rewrite text more clearly and has reference examples of the improved versions. It wants the model's output to resemble those examples. Which metric should it use?
explanation:
ROUGE measures the n-gram and sequence overlap between the model's output and the reference examples, so it directly captures how closely the output resembles those improved versions.
Perplexity reflects language-modeling fit, semantic robustness measures stability under input changes, and latency measures speed; none compares output against reference examples.

text: A company's image-generation model keeps producing pictures unrelated to the prompts, and the team wants to adjust its prompting to cut down on these. Which technique helps?
options: Use negative prompts that state what to exclude
explanation:
Negative prompts explicitly tell the model what to leave out, constraining generation so fewer off-topic elements appear.
Adding example images or using zero-shot prompts gives no instruction about what to avoid, and making prompts more open-ended increases drift rather than reducing it.

text: An electronics retailer wants an LLM to write short, feature-focused product descriptions. Which prompt-engineering approach works best?
options: Write one generic prompt for all products and manually edit each output
Create category-specific prompts that highlight key features and specify the output format and length
List every product attribute in a single prompt and ask for a description
Ask the model for the most creative description it can produce, then trim it
explanation:
Category-specific prompts that call out the key features and set the format and length steer the model to consistent, concise, feature-focused descriptions with little rework.
A single generic prompt needs heavy manual editing; listing every attribute produces long, unfocused text; asking for maximum creativity and trimming wastes effort and drifts from the required style.

text: An insurance company wants an AI application that lets employees look up open claims, retrieve the details of a specific claim, and pull the claim's documents. Which solution fits best?
options: Use Agents for Amazon Bedrock with Amazon Fraud Detector
Use Agents for Amazon Bedrock with Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases
Use an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base on its own, without an agent
Train a new ML model with Amazon SageMaker AI
explanation:
Agents for Amazon Bedrock carry out the multi-step actions (looking up claims, extracting details, fetching documents) and call an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base to retrieve the claim data, which together meet all three needs.
Pairing the agent with Amazon Fraud Detector adds fraud scoring rather than document retrieval; a knowledge base alone can retrieve content but cannot orchestrate the lookups and actions; training a new model with Amazon SageMaker AI is far more effort than needed.

text: An analyst adds an instruction to a prompt on Amazon Bedrock asking the model to show its work and explain each step while solving math problems. Which prompt-engineering technique is being used?
explanation:
Chain-of-thought prompting asks the model to lay out its intermediate reasoning step by step, which is exactly what instructing it to show its work does, improving accuracy on math problems.
Few-shot prompting supplies worked examples; tree of thoughts explores several reasoning branches in parallel; zero-shot prompting gives only an instruction with no reasoning scaffold.

text: A company needs higher-quality answers from a large language model (LLM) on complex problems that require detailed, step-by-step reasoning. Which prompt-engineering technique fits?
explanation:
Chain-of-thought prompting guides the model to produce its reasoning as a series of logical steps within the response, which improves answer quality on complex problems.
Directional stimulus prompting steers output with hints or keywords; prompt chaining sends several separate prompts in sequence; least-to-most prompting decomposes a task into ordered subproblems but is a distinct technique from generating an in-line reasoning chain.

text: A retailer runs an AI assistant that helps agents answer frequently asked questions, but the questions keep changing. Agents type a question and need an up-to-date generated answer at the lowest cost. Which approach fits?
options: Use Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) with prompt engineering
Fine-tune the model on a recurring schedule
Pre-train the model on the FAQ data and benchmark it
Embed the full FAQ set into the system prompt
explanation:
RAG retrieves the most relevant, current information at query time and prompt engineering shapes the response, so the assistant stays accurate as questions change without repeated training cost.
Scheduled fine-tuning and pre-training both require recurring, expensive training runs; embedding the full FAQ set into every prompt drives up token costs and does not scale as the FAQ grows.

text: A company wants more accurate answers from a generative AI application on Amazon Bedrock and wants the cheapest way to get them. Which approach fits?
options: Apply model distillation to the FM
explanation:
Prompt engineering improves accuracy by refining the instructions and context with no training cost, making it the cheapest option.
Fine-tuning adds training cost and data preparation, model distillation requires a separate training process to build a smaller model, and retraining from scratch is the most expensive approach of all.

text: An application summarizes books of varying lengths but fails on some of the longer ones. What is the most likely cause?
options: The temperature is set too high
The input exceeds the model's maximum context window
The maximum output length is set too low
The model does not support few-shot prompting
explanation:
A model can only process a limited number of input tokens, so a book whose length exceeds the maximum context window cannot be handled in one pass, which explains why only the longer books fail.
A high temperature changes randomness, not capacity; a low maximum output length would shorten every summary rather than fail on selected books; and few-shot support is irrelevant to summarizing one long input.

text: An airline wants a text chatbot for flight schedules, bookings, and payments, built on large language models (LLMs) plus a knowledge base, with the LEAST development effort. Which solution fits?
options: Train models with Amazon SageMaker Autopilot
Fine-tune models on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart
Build a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) agent with Amazon Bedrock
Build a custom orchestration service with AWS Lambda and a self-hosted model
explanation:
Amazon Bedrock lets the team combine an LLM with a knowledge base using RAG to deliver accurate, current answers with minimal development effort.
SageMaker Autopilot trains traditional ML models from tabular data; fine-tuning on SageMaker JumpStart needs data preparation and a training run; building a custom Lambda orchestration layer over a self-hosted model is the most work of all.

text: Which statement describes a genuine risk or limitation of prompt engineering for a generative AI model?
options: Prompt engineering guarantees deterministic outputs, so validation is unnecessary
Prompt engineering can expose the model to prompt injection attacks
Prompt engineering permanently updates the model's weights with each prompt
Prompt engineering eliminates all risk of data poisoning and model hijacking
explanation:
A real limitation of prompt engineering is that crafted inputs can still be exploited through prompt injection, where an attacker manipulates the prompt to change the model's behavior.
Prompt engineering does not make outputs deterministic or remove the need for validation, it does not update the model's weights (that is fine-tuning), and it cannot eliminate risks such as data poisoning or model hijacking.

text: A publisher's Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) application must feel near real time, while new articles are published daily. Which two pipeline steps can run as offline batch jobs?
options: Generating embeddings for each incoming user query
Generating embeddings for the published content
Ranking and returning results for a user's query
Building or updating the vector search index
Detecting the language of each user query
explanation:
Generating content embeddings and building or updating the search index depend only on the documents, so they can run in periodic batches as new articles arrive, off the real-time path.
Generating embeddings for a user query, ranking and returning results, and detecting a query's language all happen per request and must run in real time.

text: Which technique decomposes a complex task into smaller subtasks that are sent to a large language model (LLM) in sequence, each building on the last?
explanation:
Prompt chaining breaks a complex task into smaller subtasks and feeds them to the LLM one after another, with each step using the output of the previous one.
Chain-of-thought reasons step by step within a single response; tree of thoughts explores multiple reasoning branches; few-shot prompting supplies examples rather than sequencing subtasks.

text: An AI practitioner must improve the accuracy of a text-generation model that depends on rapidly changing inventory data. Which technique helps most?
options: Fine-tune the model on historical inventory data
explanation:
RAG fetches the current inventory data at inference time and conditions generation on it, so the output reflects the latest information and stays accurate without retraining.
Fine-tuning on historical data, transfer learning, and continuous pre-training on snapshots all bake data in at training time, so they go stale as the inventory keeps changing.

text: In a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) workflow, what is the main purpose of chunking documents?
options: To reduce the cost of storing the documents
To improve the relevance of passages retrieved from the vector index
To speed up training of the model
To avoid having to generate embeddings for the documents
explanation:
Splitting documents into smaller, semantically coherent chunks lets the retriever return only the most relevant segments for a query, improving the relevance of the context passed to the model.
Chunking is not aimed at lowering storage cost, it does not speed up model training, and chunked text is still embedded, so it does not avoid generating embeddings.

text: Which statement describes an advantage of Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) for natural language processing (NLP) tasks?
options: It speeds up training of the underlying language model
It reduces the model's parameter count to save memory
It draws on external knowledge sources to produce more accurate, informative responses
explanation:
RAG retrieves relevant external documents at inference time and conditions generation on them, enriching responses with up-to-date, domain-specific knowledge without retraining the model.
RAG does not speed up training or reduce the model's parameter count, and it does not make a generative model's outputs deterministic.

text: Which technique trains an AI model on a labeled dataset so it adapts to a specific industry's terminology and requirements?
explanation:
Fine-tuning continues training a pre-trained model on a labeled, domain-specific dataset so it learns the industry's terminology and task requirements directly from that data.
Continuous pre-training relies on large unlabeled data; in-context learning adds examples at inference time without training; model distillation transfers knowledge into a smaller model rather than adapting it to a labeled domain dataset.

text: A team built an agent with Amazon Bedrock Agents and wants to improve its accuracy by giving it a few specific examples. Which approach fits?
options: Fine-tune the underlying model on the examples
Add the examples to the agent's advanced prompts
Add the examples to an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base
Create a guardrail that includes the examples
explanation:
Adding the specific input-output examples to the agent's advanced prompts is few-shot prompting, which steers the agent toward more accurate behavior with no retraining or extra services.
Fine-tuning the model is far heavier for a handful of examples; a knowledge base supplies retrieved context rather than behavioral examples; a guardrail enforces safety policies, not example-driven accuracy.

text: A company will use instruction-based fine-tuning to adapt a foundation model (FM) to its domain. How should it prepare the training data?
options: Assemble a large unlabeled domain corpus and continue pre-training
Create instruction-and-response (question-and-answer) pairs for the domain
Build a vector index of the documents for retrieval
Collect human preference rankings of model outputs
explanation:
Instruction-based fine-tuning needs instruction-response examples, so curating domain-specific question-and-answer pairs teaches the model how to interpret domain queries and produce correct answers.
An unlabeled corpus is for continuous pre-training; a vector index supports RAG rather than training; human preference rankings are the data used for RLHF, not instruction tuning.

text: Which metric is commonly used to evaluate how well a foundation model (FM) performs on text summarization?
explanation:
ROUGE measures the overlap between a generated summary and reference summaries, which makes it the standard metric for summarization quality.
F1 is a classification metric, MSE measures regression error, and BLEU is built for machine translation; none targets summarization.

text: What is a benefit of fine-tuning a foundation model (FM)?
options: It lets the model pull in external data at inference time
It improves the model's performance on a specific task by further training it on task data
It compresses the model to reduce size and speed up inference
It refreshes the model's general knowledge by pre-training on newer data
explanation:
Fine-tuning updates the model's weights using task-relevant data, sharpening its accuracy and relevance on that specific task.
Pulling in external data at inference time describes RAG; compressing the model describes distillation; refreshing general knowledge with newer pre-training describes continuous pre-training.

text: What are two primary use cases for storing embeddings in a vector database such as Amazon OpenSearch Service?
explanation:
Semantic search and similarity-based recommendations both rely on nearest neighbor comparison of embeddings, which is exactly what a vector database provides.
Exact keyword matching is lexical rather than semantic, and primary-key lookups and scheduled batch ETL are standard database operations that do not use vector similarity.

text: For AI applications, which two capabilities of Amazon Aurora with the pgvector extension are the most important?
explanation:
Vector similarity search lets the application find the most semantically related content, which is the core retrieval step in tasks such as RAG, and the ability to combine vectors with structured data means those searches can run alongside existing relational records in the same database, so together these two capabilities are what make Aurora with pgvector valuable for AI workloads.
Standard SQL operations are a general database capability that is not specific to AI applications. Web hosting and email handling are not functions of Amazon Aurora at all and are unrelated to vector storage or AI workloads.

text: A company wants a large language model (LLM) to write product descriptions and plans to include several example descriptions that follow a fixed format in the prompt. Which prompt-engineering technique does this use?
explanation:
Few-shot prompting places several examples in the prompt so the model learns the pattern and format and generates new descriptions in the same style, without any training.
Zero-shot prompting supplies no examples, one-shot prompting supplies only a single example, and role prompting assigns a persona but does not provide formatted examples.

text: A grocery chain wants a chatbot that checks live inventory and tells shoppers where a product is located in the store. Which prompt-engineering technique should it use?
explanation:
ReAct prompting interleaves the model's reasoning with explicit actions, such as calling a live inventory API, then uses the returned data to answer, which is what is needed to check stock and report a product's location in real time.
Few-shot, chain-of-thought, and zero-shot prompting shape reasoning or supply examples but provide no mechanism to call an external system for live data.

text: A company measures its translation tool by comparing the tool's outputs with human translations of the same documents. Which evaluation strategy should it use?
options: Use ROUGE to estimate the absolute translation quality of the two methods
Use the Bilingual Evaluation Understudy (BLEU) score to estimate the relative translation quality of the two methods
Use the Bilingual Evaluation Understudy (BLEU) score to estimate the absolute translation quality of the two methods
Use ROUGE to estimate the relative translation quality of the two methods
explanation:
BLEU measures n-gram overlap against reference translations, so applying it to both the tool's outputs and the human outputs on the same documents gives comparable scores for judging which method is relatively better.
BLEU produces a relative comparison, not an absolute quality measure, so the absolute-BLEU option is wrong; ROUGE is built for summarization, making it the wrong metric for comparing translations.

text: A company's generative AI application uses a pre-trained foundation model (FM) on Amazon Bedrock and wants its answers to include the company's own information, at the lowest cost. Which solution fits?
options: Deploy a custom model on Amazon Bedrock
Fine-tune the FM on the company information
explanation:
Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases index and retrieve the company's documents at inference time and inject relevant context into the prompt (RAG), adding the information cheaply with no training.
Deploying a custom model and fine-tuning the FM both add training cost; Amazon Bedrock Agents orchestrate tasks but do not, on their own, supply document context.

text: A company is building an HR-policy chatbot on a large language model (LLM) with a large set of digital documents and wants to optimize the quality of its answers. Which technique fits best?
options: Fine-tune the model on the policy documents
explanation:
RAG retrieves precise, current passages from the policy documents at query time and grounds the chatbot's answers in them, optimizing accuracy without overloading the context window.
Setting the temperature to 1 only adds randomness; fine-tuning is costly and goes stale as policies change; decreasing the token size drops the context the model needs.

text: An education company trains a custom large language model (LLM) for teenagers and wants the output to match their style, including creative spelling and shorthand. Which metric should it use to assess the output against reference examples?
explanation:
BLEU measures surface-level n-gram overlap between the model's output and reference text, so it is suited to checking how closely the model reproduces the exact teen-style spelling and shorthand.
BERTScore measures semantic similarity rather than surface forms; perplexity measures language-modeling fit; F1 is a classification metric.

text: A bank is building a chatbot to answer account-opening questions using public bank documents on Amazon Bedrock with prompt engineering. Which technique fits?
explanation:
Few-shot prompting supplies several example questions and answers drawn from the bank documents, guiding the model to produce accurate, well-formatted responses without training.
Directional stimulus prompting steers output with hints, zero-shot prompting provides no examples, and one-shot prompting provides only a single example.

text: A company wants a chatbot for employee policy questions; policies change often and answers must reflect updates in near real time. Which solution fits?
options: Fine-tune a large language model (LLM) on the policy text with Amazon SageMaker AI
Create a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) workflow with Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases
Continuously pre-train an LLM on the policy documents
Build a custom application with Amazon Q Business
explanation:
A RAG workflow with Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases retrieves the latest policy documents at query time, so the chatbot reflects updates in near real time without retraining.
Fine-tuning and continuous pre-training must be re-run whenever policies change; a custom Amazon Q Business application is more development effort and is not the targeted way to keep the answers current here.

text: A company uses supervised learning to train a model on a small labeled dataset for a specific task. Which step of the foundation model (FM) lifecycle is this?
explanation:
Fine-tuning continues training a pre-trained model on a small labeled dataset for a target task, which is exactly the supervised step described.
Pre-training and continuous pre-training use large, mostly unlabeled data; deployment puts the finished model into production. None of these is the supervised, task-specific training step.

text: A company wants to label training data with human feedback to fine-tune a foundation model (FM) but does not want to build labeling tools or manage a workforce. Which AWS service or feature fits?
explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth Plus is a fully managed labeling service that uses a human workforce, so the company gets human-labeled data without building labeling tools or managing labelers.
SageMaker Data Wrangler prepares and transforms data, SageMaker Clarify detects bias and explains predictions, and SageMaker Autopilot automatically builds models. None of these provides managed human labeling.

text: A media streaming company wants natural-language image search with similarity and nearest neighbor queries, backed by a vector database. Which AWS service fits?
explanation:
Amazon OpenSearch Service supports vector storage with similarity (nearest neighbor) search, which is what natural-language image search and filtering require.
Amazon DynamoDB (key-value) and Amazon RDS for MySQL (relational) lack native vector similarity search, and Amazon Personalize generates recommendations rather than serving as a general vector store.

text: A company is comparing several large language models (LLMs) for text summarization and needs a metric for summary quality. Which metric fits?
explanation:
ROUGE measures the overlap between generated summaries and reference summaries, making it the standard metric for summarization quality.
BLEU is built for translation, AUC is a classification metric, and perplexity measures language-modeling fit; none is designed for summary quality.

text: A company needs an AI solution that produces both images and text descriptions for a product catalog and is comparing foundation models (FMs) by the output types each supports. Which FM characteristic is it evaluating?
explanation:
Modality describes the input and output types an FM supports, such as text or images, so evaluating whether a model can output both images and text descriptions is an assessment of modality.
Latency is response speed, context window length is how much input and output fit, and multilingual support concerns languages; none describes the output types a model can generate.

text: An online retailer wants to evaluate a model that labels each customer review as positive, negative, or neutral. Which model evaluation task type fits this requirement?
explanation:
Classification assigns each input to one of a fixed set of predefined categories, so sorting every customer review into one of three sentiment labels (positive, negative, or neutral) is a classification task and is evaluated with classification metrics.
Open-ended text generation produces free-form text from a prompt and has no fixed set of output labels. Text summarization condenses longer text into a shorter version rather than assigning it to a category. Question and answer returns a response to a posed question rather than placing the input into predefined sentiment categories.

text: Which AWS service stores embeddings in a vector database for use with foundation models (FMs) and Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)?
explanation:
Amazon OpenSearch Service provides a vector database that stores and searches embeddings, which is what powers RAG workflows and integrations with foundation models.
Amazon S3 is object storage, Amazon DynamoDB is a key-value database, and Amazon Redshift is a data warehouse; none offers native vector search over embeddings.

text: A company is building a generative AI solution on Amazon Bedrock and needs a service that provides vector database storage and vector search. Which AWS service fits?
explanation:
Amazon OpenSearch Service supports vector storage and similarity search over embeddings, so it can back a generative AI solution on Amazon Bedrock.
Amazon DynamoDB is a key-value database, Amazon ElastiCache is an in-memory cache, and Amazon Redshift is a data warehouse; none provides native vector database and search capabilities.

text: When designing prompts for a generative AI model, which two practices are important?
options: Maximize prompt length regardless of relevance
Use ambiguous wording to encourage creativity
Include relevant examples when they help
Omit instructions and rely on model defaults
explanation:
Clear context and instructions tell the model what is expected, and relevant examples (few-shot prompting) guide it toward the desired output format and style, so both improve prompt quality.
Maximizing length regardless of relevance, using ambiguous wording, and omitting instructions all add noise or ambiguity and degrade the model's responses.

text: Which two metrics are commonly used to evaluate the output quality of generative AI models?
options: Bilingual Evaluation Understudy (BLEU) score for translation quality
Request throughput in requests per second
Recall-Oriented Understudy for Gisting Evaluation (ROUGE) score for summarization quality
explanation:
BLEU assesses translation quality and ROUGE assesses summarization quality by comparing generated text to reference text, so both measure the quality of generative output.
GPU memory usage, request throughput, and model parameter count are infrastructure and model-size metrics that say nothing about output quality.

text: Which two capabilities of Amazon OpenSearch Service are most relevant for AI/ML workloads?
options: k-NN nearest neighbor search over vectors
Storing and indexing embeddings as a vector database
explanation:
k-NN nearest neighbor search and storing and indexing embeddings as a vector database underpin AI/ML tasks such as semantic search and RAG.
BM25 keyword search is lexical rather than semantic, geospatial queries handle location data, and OpenSearch does not perform model training.

text: A company wants an AI assistant that can evaluate specific data sources, call external APIs, and then generate, compare, and prioritize response options. Which Amazon Bedrock feature fits?
explanation:
Amazon Bedrock Agents orchestrate multi-step tasks, including calling external APIs and generating, comparing, and prioritizing response options, which matches all of the stated needs.
Prompt Management versions prompts, Knowledge Bases supply retrieved context, and Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation scores models; none orchestrates API calls and decision-making on its own.

text: In generative AI, what distinguishes zero-shot, one-shot, and few-shot prompting?
options: The number of examples provided in the prompt
The number of reasoning steps the model takes
The amount of data used to fine-tune the model
explanation:
These terms describe how many examples are placed in the prompt: zero-shot gives none, one-shot gives a single example, and few-shot gives a small set, all without retraining the model.
They do not refer to the model architecture, the number of reasoning steps, or the amount of fine-tuning data, which are unrelated to how many in-prompt examples are supplied.

text: An ML team is training a foundation model (FM) and wants to push its accuracy up to a required threshold. What should the team do?
explanation:
Increasing the number of epochs lets the model train over more passes of the data, which generally improves accuracy until it reaches the target level.
Decreasing the epochs gives the model less training and tends to lower accuracy. Decreasing the batch size mainly affects training dynamics and memory use rather than reliably raising accuracy toward a target. Temperature is an inference parameter that controls output randomness and has no effect on training accuracy.

text: A cosmetics brand wants a pre-trained generative AI model to write campaign copy that fits its brand voice and messaging. What should the team do?
options: Add more layers to the model's architecture to increase its complexity
Craft clear, well-structured prompts that provide instructions and context to guide the model's output
Tune the model's architecture and hyperparameters to improve its overall performance
Collect a large, diverse dataset and pre-train a new generative model from scratch
explanation:
Crafting clear prompts with instructions and context guides the pre-trained model to generate content that matches the brand voice, without modifying the model itself.
Adding layers or tuning the architecture and hyperparameters means re-engineering or retraining the model, which is unnecessary and costly here. Pre-training a new model from scratch is even more resource-intensive and is not needed to align output with brand voice.

text: A consultancy must choose an Amazon Bedrock model for internal use, and its analysts care about the writing style of the answers. How should the firm choose the model?
options: Evaluate the models with built-in prompt datasets
Choose the model based on public model leaderboards
Evaluate the models with a human workforce using custom prompt datasets
Compare the models using the InvocationLatency runtime metric in Amazon CloudWatch
explanation:
Using a human workforce to evaluate the models against custom prompt datasets captures subjective style preferences that automated scores miss, so it best identifies the model whose responses match what employees prefer.
Built-in prompt datasets and public leaderboards measure general performance, not the company specific style preference. The InvocationLatency metric in Amazon CloudWatch measures response speed, not response style.

text: A news app runs sentiment analysis with a large language model (LLM) on Amazon Bedrock and wants the same input to yield steadier results. Which inference parameter should it change?
options: Reduce the maximum number of output tokens
explanation:
Lowering the temperature reduces randomness in token selection, making the model outputs more deterministic and consistent for the same input.
Raising the temperature increases randomness and variability. Changing the maximum generation length or reducing the number of output tokens only affects response length, not how consistent the responses are.

text: A team needs to check how accurately its image-classification foundation model (FM) performs. Which strategy should the team use?
options: Count the number of layers in the model's neural network
Calculate the total cost of the resources the model uses
Check the color accuracy of the images the model processes
Measure the model's accuracy on a predefined benchmark dataset
explanation:
Measuring the model's accuracy against a predefined benchmark dataset is the standard way to assess classification accuracy, because performance is compared against known correct labels.
Counting neural-network layers describes architecture, not accuracy. Calculating total resource cost measures expense. Checking the color accuracy of processed images is unrelated to classification correctness.

text: A telecom company's chatbot uses a large language model (LLM) on Amazon Bedrock for intent detection, and the team wants to improve accuracy with few-shot learning. What data does the team need?
options: Pairs of user messages and their correct user intents
Pairs of user messages and their correct chatbot responses
Pairs of chatbot responses and their correct user intents
Pairs of user intents and their correct chatbot responses
explanation:
Few-shot learning supplies the model with example input-output pairs for the task, and intent detection maps a user message to an intent, so the company needs pairs of user messages and their correct user intents.
Pairs that involve chatbot responses, whether messages-to-responses, responses-to-intents, or intents-to-responses, train the wrong mapping and do not demonstrate how to detect a user intent from a message.

text: During a red-team test of a foundation model (FM), an engineer tries to get past its safety filters so it produces harmful text. What is this technique called?
options: Fuzzing the training data to find vulnerabilities
explanation:
Jailbreaking is the attempt to circumvent or disable a model built-in safety controls so it produces restricted or harmful content, which is exactly what the engineer is doing.
Fuzzing the training data probes for vulnerabilities by feeding malformed inputs during development, not by bypassing safety filters. Authorized penetration testing is a sanctioned security assessment. A denial-of-service attack targets availability rather than defeating content safeguards.

text: A team is building a conversational search feature and needs a database that can store generative AI embeddings as vectors and run similarity queries over them. Which AWS service meets this requirement?
explanation:
Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL supports the pgvector extension, which stores, indexes, and runs similarity queries over vector embeddings, making it suitable for storing and querying embeddings as vectors.
Amazon Athena is a serverless query service for data in Amazon S3. Amazon Redshift is a data warehouse for analytics. Amazon EMR runs big-data processing frameworks. None of these is designed to store and query vector embeddings for similarity search.

text: How can a team determine whether a foundation model (FM) effectively meets its business objectives?
options: Evaluate the model's performance on benchmark datasets
Assess how well the model aligns with the specific use cases it must support
Analyze the model's architecture and hyperparameters
Measure the computational resources the model needs for deployment
explanation:
Assessing how well the model aligns with the specific use cases it must support shows whether its outputs solve the real business problems, which is how you tell if it meets business objectives.
Benchmark performance measures general accuracy, not business fit. Analyzing architecture and hyperparameters is a technical detail unrelated to business value. Measuring computational resources addresses cost and feasibility, not whether the objectives are met.

text: A company wants to keep its foundation model (FM) current by regularly retraining it on the latest data. Which training strategy meets this requirement?
explanation:
Continuous pre-training periodically ingests the latest data and updates the model's weights, so the foundation model stays current without retraining from scratch each time.
Batch learning processes data in fixed batches but is not a strategy for ongoing model refresh. Static training produces a one-time fixed model that does not update. Latent training is not a recognized training strategy.

text: A company's large language model (LLM) keeps producing hallucinations. Which change can reduce them?
options: Decrease the temperature inference parameter for the model
Use Agents for Amazon Bedrock to supervise the model's training
Preprocess the data to remove any data that causes hallucinations
Switch to a foundation model (FM) that is trained never to hallucinate
explanation:
Lowering the temperature parameter reduces the randomness of the model's token selection, so it relies on higher-probability outputs and is less likely to produce hallucinated content.
Agents for Amazon Bedrock orchestrate tasks and do not supervise training. You cannot reliably identify and remove specific data that causes hallucinations through preprocessing. No foundation model is guaranteed never to hallucinate, so switching models does not solve the problem.

text: How does top-p (nucleus) sampling differ from temperature-based sampling?
options: It samples from the smallest possible set of tokens
It samples only from the set of tokens whose probabilities add up to p
It works only with specific model architectures
explanation:
Top-p (nucleus) sampling dynamically restricts the candidate tokens to the smallest set whose cumulative probability reaches p and then samples from that set, which adapts the choice of tokens to the probability distribution at each step.
It does not fix the token set to the smallest possible size regardless of probabilities. It does not produce deterministic output, since it still samples. It is not limited to specific model architectures.

text: A retailer has 100 high-quality agent-customer conversations and wants its chatbot's replies to match the company's tone. Which solution meets this requirement?
options: Use Amazon Personalize to generate the responses
Create an Amazon Bedrock fine-tuning job
Create an Amazon SageMaker HyperPod pre-training job
Host the model on Amazon SageMaker AI and apply TensorRT to optimize LLM inference
explanation:
An Amazon Bedrock fine-tuning job adapts a foundation model on the company's own example conversations, teaching it the company's tone so the chatbot reflects it in responses.
Amazon Personalize is a recommendation service, not a way to style chatbot text. A SageMaker HyperPod pre-training job is for large-scale pre-training from scratch, which is overkill for 100 examples. Hosting the model and applying TensorRT optimizes inference speed, not response tone.

text: An AI practitioner is comparing top-p (nucleus) sampling with temperature-based sampling. What distinguishes top-p sampling?
options: It works only with certain model architectures
It always returns the same output for a given prompt
It limits sampling to exactly one token each step
It samples from the smallest set of top tokens whose probabilities sum to p
explanation:
Top-p (nucleus) sampling chooses the smallest set of highest-probability tokens whose cumulative probability reaches p and samples from that set, adapting the candidate pool to the distribution at each step rather than using a fixed cutoff.
It is not restricted to particular model architectures. It still samples, so it does not return identical output every time. It does not limit selection to a single token.

text: A company is adding a large language model (LLM) to its app and needs responses that are as deterministic and stable as possible. Which solution meets this requirement?
options: Add "make your response deterministic" to the end of the prompt before sending it
Set the temperature parameter to 1 when submitting the prompt
Set the temperature parameter to 0 when submitting the prompt
Add "make your response deterministic" to the start of the prompt before sending it
explanation:
Setting the temperature to 0 forces greedy decoding, so the model selects the most probable next token every time and produces deterministic, stable outputs.
Setting the temperature to 1 keeps full randomness, which is the opposite of deterministic. Adding an instruction like make your response deterministic at the start or end of the prompt does not control the sampling process and will not reliably make output deterministic.

text: Which large language model (LLM) parameter sets how many candidate next tokens the model considers at each generation step?
explanation:
The Top K parameter limits sampling at each step to the K most probable next tokens, so it directly controls how many candidate tokens the model considers when generating each token.
Maximum tokens caps the total length of the output, not the candidate pool at each step. Temperature adjusts the randomness of the distribution rather than the number of candidates. Batch size concerns how many inputs are processed together, not token selection.

text: An AI practitioner wants a large language model (LLM) to produce more diverse and creative output. How should the practitioner adjust an inference parameter?
explanation:
Raising the temperature flattens the model's probability distribution and increases the chance of selecting less-likely tokens, which produces more varied and creative responses.
Decreasing the Top K value narrows the candidate tokens and makes output more focused, not more diverse. Increasing the response length only makes output longer. Decreasing the prompt length reduces context and does not increase creativity.

text: A company will fine-tune a large language model (LLM) on Amazon Bedrock to refine the style of its app's output messages. Which type of data does the company need?
options: Paired samples of input messages and their corresponding output messages
Separate, unpaired samples of input messages and output messages
explanation:
Fine-tuning to refine output style requires paired examples of input messages and their corresponding output messages, so the model learns the mapping from input to the desired styled output.
Samples of only input messages or only output messages lack the input-to-output relationship the model must learn. Separate, unpaired samples do not show which output goes with which input, so the model cannot learn the styling.

text: Which two parameters are commonly used to control the diversity of a generative AI model's output?
explanation:
Top-k sampling limits selection to the k most likely next tokens, and Top-p (nucleus) sampling selects from the smallest set of tokens whose probabilities sum to p; both adjust the candidate pool to balance diversity and quality of generated text.
Model size, training dataset size, and hardware configuration affect a model's capability, cost, or speed, but they are not runtime parameters that control output diversity.

text: A design team uses an image-generation foundation model (FM) on Amazon Bedrock and wants to control how detailed or abstract each generated image is. Which model parameter should they adjust?
explanation:
The generation step parameter sets how many refinement steps the model runs while creating an image; more steps yield more detailed images and fewer steps yield more abstract ones, so it controls the level of detail.
A model checkpoint selects a saved version of the model, not the detail of a single image. Batch size sets how many images are produced at once. Token length applies to text generation, not image detail.

text: A team generates images with an Amazon Nova Canvas model and needs to keep specific items out of the results. Which solution meets this requirement?
explanation:
A negative prompt specifies the items or characteristics the model should avoid, so it keeps the unwanted items out of the generated images.
A higher temperature only adds randomness. A more detailed prompt describes what to include but does not reliably exclude specific items. Switching to another foundation model does not provide a mechanism to exclude items.

text: A company is building a generative AI tool and will customize a foundation model (FM) with its internal documents. Which approach meets this requirement?
explanation:
Continued pre-training further trains a foundation model on the company's internal documents, so the model adapts to the company's domain and content.
Classification and regression are supervised ML tasks, not ways to customize an FM on documents. Distillation transfers knowledge from a larger model to a smaller one rather than adapting a model to internal documents.

text: A research group wants several scientists to manually compare the outputs of different generative AI models for a defined prompt. Which solution meets this requirement?
options: Use automatic evaluation on Amazon Personalize
Use model evaluation on Amazon Bedrock
Use content moderation on Amazon Rekognition
Use sentiment analysis on Amazon Comprehend
explanation:
Amazon Bedrock model evaluation supports human-based evaluation, so a team of scientists can review and compare the models' outputs against the group's prompt and criteria.
Amazon Personalize provides recommendations. Amazon Rekognition does image and video content moderation. Amazon Comprehend does NLP tasks such as sentiment analysis. None of these provides human evaluation of generative model output.

text: A support center rolls out a large language model (LLM) chatbot to cut down how many steps agents take when answering customer questions. Which business metric best shows whether the chatbot is making a difference?
explanation:
Average call duration directly reflects how much the chatbot reduces the steps agents take to resolve questions, so tracking it measures the chatbot's business impact.
Corporate social responsibility and regulatory compliance are organizational concerns unrelated to how quickly agents resolve customer questions. Website engagement rate measures online visitor behavior, not call center efficiency.

text: For AI workloads, what is the main benefit of pairing Amazon Aurora with the pgvector extension?
options: It enables vector similarity search inside a relational database
explanation:
Amazon Aurora with the pgvector extension enables vector similarity search inside a relational database, so embeddings can be stored alongside structured data and queried with SQL while keeping relational features.
Aurora does not automatically generate AI models or provide pre-trained language models. Serverless capacity is a deployment option but is not the primary advantage of pgvector for AI applications.

text: A company runs several generative AI applications on Amazon Bedrock and wants to version its prompts, compare different prompt variants, and roll back to a previous version if quality drops. Which Amazon Bedrock feature meets these requirements?
explanation:
Amazon Bedrock Prompt Management lets teams create, version, and manage prompt templates, compare variants, and roll back to earlier versions, providing the lifecycle controls the company needs to maintain prompt quality across its applications.
Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases index and retrieve documents for RAG workflows. Amazon Bedrock Guardrails filter harmful or unwanted content. Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation scores and compares model performance. None of these manages prompt versions or supports rollback.

text: A company deployed an AI assistant on Amazon Bedrock to handle customer service requests. It wants to measure how effectively the assistant resolves customer issues without escalation. Which metric best captures this?
explanation:
Task completion rate measures the percentage of customer requests the assistant fully resolves without needing human escalation, directly reflecting how effectively it meets the business objective of handling service requests autonomously.
BLEU score measures translation quality by comparing generated text to references. Perplexity measures how well a language model predicts text. Model parameter count describes model size. None of these measures whether the assistant successfully completes customer tasks.

text: Which two metrics are examples of business-alignment metrics for evaluating AI applications?
explanation:
User satisfaction measures how well the AI application meets end-user expectations, and cost per interaction measures the operational expense of each user engagement, both of which directly align with business objectives and are defined as business-alignment metrics for AI applications.
BERTScore and ROUGE score are technical metrics that measure the quality of generated text against references rather than business outcomes. Model training time is an operational metric about how long training takes and says nothing about whether the application achieves its business goals.

text: A company is building a knowledge graph that also needs to store vector embeddings and run similarity searches over them alongside graph traversals. Which AWS database service supports both graph queries and vector search?
explanation:
Amazon Neptune is a graph database that also supports vector similarity search, allowing the company to store embeddings alongside knowledge graph relationships and run both graph traversals and nearest-neighbor queries in the same database.
Amazon DynamoDB is a key-value and document database without native graph or vector search capabilities. Amazon Redshift is a data warehouse for analytics. Amazon ElastiCache is an in-memory caching service. None of these combines graph queries with vector similarity search.

text: A company generates long-form marketing content with a foundation model and wants to evaluate quality at scale without relying on human reviewers. Which evaluation approach uses another large language model to score the outputs?
explanation:
LLM-as-a-judge uses a separate large language model to evaluate and score the outputs of another model against defined criteria, providing scalable quality assessment without requiring human reviewers for every output.
BLEU scoring compares generated text to reference translations using n-gram overlap and requires pre-written references. Benchmark dataset comparison evaluates against fixed test sets with known answers. A/B testing requires live users to compare variants. None of these uses another LLM to judge output quality.

text: A company deployed a RAG-based customer support assistant and wants to evaluate whether the retrieval component returns relevant documents for user queries. Which approach should the team use?
options: Measure the model's perplexity on a held-out dataset
Compare retrieved passages against known-correct source documents for a set of test queries
Count the total number of API calls made to Amazon Bedrock
Measure the BLEU score of the model's outputs
explanation:
Evaluating a RAG application requires assessing whether the retrieval component returns relevant documents, which is done by comparing retrieved passages for test queries against known-correct source documents and measuring retrieval precision and recall.
Perplexity evaluates language model quality, not retrieval relevance. Counting API calls measures usage volume. BLEU score evaluates translation quality. None of these assesses the retrieval pipeline.

text: A company sends the same lengthy system prompt thousands of times daily with only the user query changing, and it wants to reduce latency and cost. Which FM selection criterion is most relevant?
explanation:
Prompt caching stores the processed representation of a repeated system prompt so the model does not re-process it on every request, reducing both latency and cost when the same prefix is sent repeatedly with only the user query varying.
Multilingual support concerns language coverage. Model complexity relates to reasoning capability. Diffusion capability applies to image generation models. None of these addresses the cost of processing a repeated prompt prefix.

text: A company needs a foundation model that can accept both text and images as input and produce text output. Which FM selection criterion determines whether a model supports this?
explanation:
Modality describes the types of input and output a model supports, such as text, images, audio, or video. A model must support multimodal input (text and images) to accept both types and produce text output.
Temperature range controls output randomness. Context window size determines how much information fits in a single prompt. Training dataset size affects model knowledge but does not determine supported input types.

text: A company runs a large foundation model on Amazon Bedrock but finds the inference cost too high. It wants a smaller, cheaper model that retains most of the large model's quality. Which customization approach meets this requirement?
explanation:
Model distillation trains a smaller student model to replicate the behavior of a larger teacher model, producing a compact model that retains most of the original's quality at lower inference cost.
RAG retrieves external documents at query time but does not reduce model size or cost. Continuous pre-training updates knowledge but does not shrink the model. In-context learning adds examples to the prompt, which actually increases token costs.

text: A travel company wants an AI system that can search flight availability, compare prices across airlines, book tickets, and send confirmation emails, all from a single customer request. Which solution meets this requirement?
options: An AI agent that orchestrates multi-step tasks using tool calls
A classification model that routes requests to departments
A recommendation engine that suggests popular flights
explanation:
